title.en: Volume 163 Biographies 88: Kong, Mu, Cui, Liu, Yan, Ma

sentences.zh: 孔穆崔柳楊馬

translations.literal: Kong, Mu, Cui, Liu, Yang, and Ma
translations.idiomatic: The Kong, Mu, Cui, Liu, Yang, and Ma Clans

translations.literal: 1.1.1 Son: Zunru
translations.idiomatic: 1.1.1 Son: Zunru

sentences.zh: 1.1.2 遵孺子 緯

translations.literal: 1.1.2 Zunru's son: Wei
translations.idiomatic: 1.1.2 Son of Zunru: Wei

translations.literal: 1.3.1 Son: Wenye
translations.idiomatic: 1.3.1 Son: Wenye

sentences.zh: 孔巢父

translations.literal: Kong Chaofu
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chaofu

sentences.zh: 孔巢父，字弱翁，孔子三十七世孫。

translations.literal: Kong Chaofu, courtesy name Ruoweng, was a thirty-seventh-generation descendant of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chaofu, styled Ruoweng, was a thirty-seventh-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 少力學，隱徂來山。

translations.literal: In youth he studied diligently and lived in seclusion on Culai Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself to study from youth and lived in retirement on Culai Mountain.

sentences.zh: 永王璘稱兵江淮，辟署幕府，不應，鏟跡民伍。

translations.literal: When Prince Yong Li Lin raised troops in the Jiang-Huai region, he was invited to serve on his staff but refused, and erased his traces among the common folk.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lin, the Prince of Yong, took up arms in the Jiang-Huai region, Chaofu was summoned to join his headquarters staff but declined, concealing himself among commoners.

sentences.zh: 璘敗，知名。

translations.literal: When Li Lin was defeated, Chaofu became well known.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Lin's defeat, Chaofu gained renown.

sentences.zh: 廣德中，李季卿宣撫江淮，薦為左衛兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: During the Guangde era, Li Jiqing, Pacification Commissioner of Jiang-Huai, recommended him as Army Adjutant in the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangde era (763–764), Li Jiqing, commissioner for pacifying the Jiang-Huai region, recommended him for the post of Left Guard Army Adjutant.

sentences.zh: 三遷庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Vice Director of the Treasury Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted three times to become Vice Director of the Treasury Bureau.

sentences.zh: 出為涇原行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Acting Chief of Staff on the Jingyuan campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as acting chief of staff on campaign in Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 累拜湖南觀察使，未行，會普王為荊襄副元帥，署行軍司馬。

translations.literal: After successive appointments as Military Commissioner of Hunan, before he took up the post, it happened that Prince Pu became Vice Commander-in-Chief of Jing-Xiang, and Chaofu was assigned as Acting Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly appointed Military Commissioner of Hunan but had not yet departed when Prince Pu was made vice commander-in-chief of the Jing-Xiang theater, and he was assigned as acting chief of staff under him.

sentences.zh: 俄而德宗狩奉天，行在擢給事中，為河中、陜、華招討使，累上破賊方略，帝嘉納。

translations.literal: Soon Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian; at the traveling court Chaofu was promoted to Supervising Secretary and made Pacification Commissioner for Hezhong, Shaanzhou, and Huazhou. He repeatedly submitted plans to defeat the rebels, and the emperor praised and adopted them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Dezong took refuge at Fengtian. At the mobile court Chaofu was promoted to Supervising Secretary and tasked with pacifying Hezhong, Shaanzhou, and Huazhou. He repeatedly submitted strategies for breaking the rebels, which the emperor warmly approved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兼御史大夫，為魏博宣慰使。

translations.literal: Before long he was also made Chief Censor and Commissioner of Consolation for Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he was additionally appointed Chief Censor and commissioner of consolation to Weibo.

sentences.zh: 巢父辯而才，及見田悅，與言君臣大義，利害逆順，開曉其眾。

translations.literal: Chaofu was eloquent and talented; when he met Tian Yue he spoke with him of the great duty between ruler and minister, of advantage and harm and what accorded or ran counter to right order, opening the understanding of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Eloquent and capable, Chaofu when he met Tian Yue expounded on the bond between sovereign and subject, on gains and losses and on right and wrong, enlightening Yue's followers.

sentences.zh: 是時，悅久不臣，下皆厭亂，雜然喜曰：「不圖今日還為王人！」

translations.literal: At that time Yue had long refused submission; his subordinates were all weary of turmoil and cried out in joy, saying: "Never did we expect that today we would again be subjects of the king!
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yue had long withheld allegiance, and his men, sick of rebellion, exclaimed with one voice: "Who would have thought that today we would again serve the throne!

sentences.zh: 酒中，悅起，自陳騎射工，曰：「陛下見用，何敵不摧！」

translations.literal: In the midst of drink Yue rose and declared his skill in horsemanship and archery, saying: "If Your Majesty would employ me, what enemy could I not crush!"
translations.idiomatic: During the drinking, Yue stood up, boasting of his mastery of horsemanship and archery: "If Your Majesty puts me to use, what foe could I not destroy!"

sentences.zh: 巢父曰：「若爾，不蚤自歸，乃一劇賊耳。」

translations.literal: Chaofu said: "If that is so, had you not submitted earlier, you would be nothing but a great rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu replied: "If that is true, then by not surrendering sooner you have been nothing but a hardened rebel."

sentences.zh: 悅曰：「能為劇賊，豈不能為功臣乎？」

translations.literal: Yue said: "If one can be a great rebel, can one not also be a meritorious minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue said: "If I can play the rebel, can I not play the loyal minister as well?"

sentences.zh: 巢父曰：「國方多虞，待子而息。」

translations.literal: Chaofu said: "The state is beset with many troubles; it waits upon you to bring them to rest."
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu said: "The realm is full of troubles just now—it is waiting for you to bring peace."

sentences.zh: 悅謝焉。

translations.literal: Yue apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue apologized.

sentences.zh: 數日，田緒殺悅，與大將邢曹俊等聽命，巢父即以緒權知軍務，紓其難。

translations.literal: Within days Tian Xu killed Yue; together with the great general Xing Caojun and others he accepted orders, and Chaofu immediately put Xu in provisional charge of military affairs, easing the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Tian Xu killed Yue. Together with the general Xing Caojun and others he submitted to imperial authority, and Chaofu at once put Xu in provisional command of the army, relieving the crisis.

sentences.zh: 李懷光據河中，帝復令巢父宣慰，罷其兵，以太子太保授之。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang held Hezhong; the emperor again sent Chaofu to console him, disbanded his army, and granted him the post of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang held the Hezhong region. The emperor again dispatched Chaofu to pacify him, stripped him of his troops, and invested him with the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 懷光素服待命，巢父不止。

translations.literal: Huaiguang had already put on mourning garb and awaited orders, but Chaofu would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was already dressed in submissive garb awaiting his orders, yet Chaofu would not leave off reading the edict.

sentences.zh: 眾忿曰：「太尉無官矣！」

translations.literal: The crowd said in anger: "The Grand Preceptor has no office left!
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers erupted in fury: "The Grand Preceptor has been stripped of his rank!

sentences.zh: 方宣詔，乃噪而合，害巢父，並殺中人啖守盈。

translations.literal: Just as the edict was being proclaimed they made a clamor and converged, killed Chaofu, and also killed the eunuch Dan Shouying.
translations.idiomatic: As the edict was being read aloud they surged forward in a riot, killed Chaofu, and also murdered the eunuch Dan Shouying.

sentences.zh: 初，巢父至，懷光以其使魏博而田悅死，疑其謀出巢父，故軍亂不肯救。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chaofu arrived, Huaiguang, because he had been sent to Weibo and Tian Yue died, suspected the plot had come from Chaofu; therefore when the army mutinied he refused to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Chaofu arrived, Huaiguang suspected he had engineered Tian Yue's death during the Weibo mission and deliberately did nothing when the troops rose up against him.

sentences.zh: 帝聞震悼，贈尚書左仆射，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he was shocked and grieved; he posthumously awarded the title of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and gave the posthumous epithet Zhong (Loyal).
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the news the emperor was stunned with grief. Chaofu was posthumously given the rank of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 詔具禮收葬，賜其家粟帛，存恤之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered full rites for interment, granted his family grain and silk, and provided them relief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him buried with full honors, granted grain and cloth to his family, and extended relief to them.

sentences.zh: 從子戣、戡、戢。

translations.literal: His nephews were Mo, Kan, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Among his nephews were Mo, Kan, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 從子 戣

translations.literal: Nephew: Mo
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Mo

sentences.zh: 戣，字君嚴，擢進士第。

translations.literal: Mo, courtesy name Junyan, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Mo, styled Junyan, passed the jinshi civil-service examination.

sentences.zh: 鄭滑盧群辟為判官，群卒，攝揔留務。

translations.literal: Lu Qun of Zheng-Hua invited him as administrative aide; when Qun died, Mo took charge of overall remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qun of Zheng-Hua district recruited him as administrative aide; when Qun died, Mo took interim charge of headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 監軍楊誌謙雅自肆，眾皆恐。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Yang Zhiqian was by nature self-indulgent; everyone was afraid of him.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor Yang Zhiqian was habitually arrogant and unrestrained, and everyone feared him.

sentences.zh: 戣邀誌謙至府，與對榻臥起，示不疑，誌謙嚴憚不敢動。

translations.literal: Mo invited Zhiqian to the headquarters, shared a couch with him for sleeping and rising, showing no suspicion; Zhiqian was in awe and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Mo invited Zhiqian to headquarters and shared his couch day and night, showing perfect trust. Awed and constrained, Zhiqian did not dare make a move.

sentences.zh: 入為侍御史，累擢諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Attending Censor and after successive promotions became Remonstrance Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court service as Attending Censor and rose through successive promotions to Remonstrance Adviser.

sentences.zh: 條上四事：一、多冗官，二、吏不奉法，三、百姓田不盡墾，四、山澤榷酤為州縣弊。

translations.literal: He submitted in detail four matters: first, too many superfluous officials; second, clerks not observing the law; third, the people's fields not fully reclaimed; fourth, state monopolies on mountains, marshes, and wine as evils of prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out four reforms in order: superfluous officials, clerks who failed to enforce the law, farmland left unopened, and the state monopolies on mountain resources and wine that plagued the prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 憲宗異其言。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was struck by his words.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong took special notice of his proposals.

sentences.zh: 中人劉希光受賕二十萬緡，抵死，吐突承璀坐厚善，逐為淮南監軍。

translations.literal: The eunuch Liu Xiguang accepted a bribe of two hundred thousand strings of cash and was punished by death; Tutu Chengcui, implicated for close friendship with him, was demoted to army supervisor in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Liu Xiguang took a bribe of two hundred thousand strings of cash and was executed. Tutu Chengcui, implicated for his close ties to Liu, was banished to serve as army supervisor in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 太子舍人李涉知帝意，投匭上言承璀有功不可棄。

translations.literal: Li She, Attendant to the Heir Apparent, knowing the emperor's intent, submitted a statement to the complaint box saying Chengcui's merits ought not be cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Li She of the Heir Apparent's household, sensing the emperor's mind, dropped a petition in the suggestion box arguing that Chengcui's past service made him worth keeping.

sentences.zh: 戣得副章，不肯受，面質讓之。

translations.literal: Mo obtained the duplicate memorial and refused to accept it, confronting She in person and rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Mo obtained a copy of the petition and refused to accept it, confronting She in person to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 涉更因左右以聞，戣劾奏涉結近幸，營罔上聽。

translations.literal: She again had those close to the throne relay word; Mo impeached She for forming ties with favored intimates and scheming to deceive what the sovereign heard.
translations.idiomatic: She then worked through court favorites to get his message to the emperor, and Mo memorialized to impeach him for cultivating the emperor's favorites and manipulating the sovereign's judgment.

sentences.zh: 有詔斥涉峽州司馬，宦寵側目，人為危之，戣自以適所誌，軒軒甚得。

translations.literal: An edict banished She to be military aide in Xia Prefecture; the eunuch favorites glared at Mo, and people thought him in danger, but Mo himself felt he had achieved his aim and was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: She was exiled to the post of military aide in Xia Prefecture. The eunuch faction glared at Mo with hostility and many thought him in grave peril, but Mo felt he had fulfilled his purpose and was quite exultant.

sentences.zh: 俄兼太子侍讀，改給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Lecturer to the Heir Apparent and changed to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed Lecturer to the Heir Apparent and transferred to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 江西觀察使李少和坐贓，獄寢不下；

translations.literal: Li Shaohe, Military Commissioner of Jiangxi, was guilty of embezzlement; the case languished without disposition;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaohe, Military Commissioner of Jiangxi, was implicated in embezzlement, but the investigation stalled without resolution;

sentences.zh: 博陵崔易簡殺從父兄，鞫狀具。

translations.literal: Cui Yijian of Boling murdered his older paternal cousin; the examination of the facts was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yijian of Boling had murdered his elder cousin; the full facts of the case had been established.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹左右之，翻其情。

translations.literal: The governor of the capital favored him and reversed the finding.
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan governor took his side and overturned the verdict.

sentences.zh: 戣慷慨論正，貶少和，殺易簡，奪尹三月俸。

translations.literal: Mo spoke forthrightly in defense of justice; Shaohe was demoted, Yijian was executed, and the governor was deprived of three months' salary.
translations.idiomatic: Mo argued forcefully for justice. Shaohe was demoted, Yijian was executed, and the governor was stripped of three months' salary.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: After a second promotion he became Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 信州刺史李位好黃老道，數祠禱，部將韋嶽告位集方士圖不軌，監軍高重謙上急變，捕位劾禁中。

translations.literal: Li Wei, prefect of Xin Prefecture, was fond of Daoist teachings of Huang-Lao and frequently performed sacrifices and prayers. His subordinate general Wei Yue reported that Wei was gathering masters of occult arts plotting rebellion. The army supervisor Gao Chongqian submitted an urgent report of emergency; Li Wei was seized and impeached within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei, prefect of Xinzhou, was devoted to Huang-Lao Daoism and frequently performed rites and prayers. His subordinate Wei Yue reported that the prefect was gathering occult practitioners to plot rebellion. Army supervisor Gao Chongqian sent an urgent report, and Li Wei was seized and placed under investigation inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 戣奏：「刺史有罪，不容系仗內，請付有司。」

translations.literal: Mo memorialized: "If a prefect is guilty, he ought not be detained within the palace precincts; I request he be handed to the proper officials.
translations.idiomatic: Mo memorialized: "A prefect who has committed a crime should not be held within the palace armed guard. I ask that he be turned over to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 詔還御史臺。

translations.literal: An edict returned the case to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the case transferred back to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 戣與三司雜治，無反狀。

translations.literal: Mo together with the Three Offices conducted a joint investigation; no signs of rebellion were found.
translations.idiomatic: Mo joined the Three Offices in a joint investigation and found no evidence of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 嶽坐誣罔誅，貶位建州司馬。

translations.literal: Yue was condemned to death for false accusation; Li Wei was demoted to military aide in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue was executed for false accusation, and Li Wei was demoted to military aide in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 中人愈怒，故出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: The eunuchs were all the more enraged; therefore Mo was sent out as prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs were further enraged, and Mo was accordingly posted out as prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 明州歲貢淡菜蚶蛤之屬，戣以為自海抵京師，道路役凡四十三萬人，奏罷之。

translations.literal: Ming Prefecture annually presented mussels, oysters, clams, and the like. Mo calculated that from the sea to the capital the road corvée totaled four hundred thirty thousand men, and memorialized to abolish the tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhou each year sent tribute of mussels, oysters, and clams. Mo reckoned that moving these from the coast to the capital required four hundred thirty thousand men in transport labor, and memorialized to end the practice.

sentences.zh: 歷大理卿、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He served successively as Minister of Justice and Chancellor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Minister of Justice and Chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 會嶺南節度使崔詠死，帝謂裴度曰：「嘗論罷蚶菜者，誰歟？

translations.literal: It happened that the Military Governor of Lingnan, Cui Yong, died. The emperor said to Pei Du: "The one who once argued to abolish the oyster tribute—who was he?
translations.idiomatic: When Military Governor Cui Yong of Lingnan died, the emperor asked Pei Du: "Who was it who once argued to abolish the oyster tribute?

sentences.zh: 今安在？

translations.literal: Where is he now?
translations.idiomatic: Where is he now?

sentences.zh: 是可往，為朕求之。」

translations.literal: He is suitable to go; find him for me.
translations.idiomatic: He would be the right man. Find him for me.

sentences.zh: 度以戣對，即拜嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: Du answered with Mo's name, and he was immediately appointed Military Governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du named Mo, and he was at once appointed military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 既至，免屬州逋負十八萬緡、米八萬斛、黃金稅歲八百兩。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he remitted one hundred eighty thousand strings of arrears owed by subordinate prefectures, eighty thousand bushels of rice, and the annual tax of eight hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he remitted arrears totaling one hundred eighty thousand strings of cash owed by subordinate prefectures, eighty thousand bushels of grain, and the annual gold tax of eight hundred ounces.

sentences.zh: 先是，屬刺史俸率三萬，又不時給，皆取部中自衣食。

translations.literal: Earlier, the salaries of subordinate prefects averaged thirty thousand each and were not paid on time; all took what they needed for food and clothing from within their jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the prefects under his command had averaged salaries of thirty thousand each, paid irregularly, and all had been feeding and clothing themselves by drawing on their jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 戣乃倍其俸，約不得為貪暴，稍以法繩之。

translations.literal: Mo then doubled their salaries, stipulating that they must not be greedy or violent, and gradually restrained them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Mo doubled their salaries, bound them not to act greedily or oppressively, and gradually reined them in with the law.

sentences.zh: 南方鬻口為貨，掠人為奴婢，戣峻為之禁。

translations.literal: In the south people sold mouths as merchandise and seized people as slaves; Mo strictly prohibited this.
translations.idiomatic: In the south people traded in human lives and seized others as slaves; Mo enforced stern prohibitions against it.

sentences.zh: 親吏得嬰兒於道，收育之，戣論以死，由是閭裏相約不敢犯。

translations.literal: An aide took an infant from the road and reared it; Mo sentenced him to death, and from this the neighborhoods mutually pledged not to dare violate the law.
translations.idiomatic: One of his personal clerks picked up a baby from the road and kept it; Mo had him sentenced to death. Thereafter neighborhoods bound themselves by agreement not to dare break the law.

sentences.zh: 士之斥南不能北歸與有罪之後百餘族，才可用，用之，稟無告者，女子為嫁遣之。

translations.literal: Among scholars banished south who could not return north and more than a hundred families of those with criminal records, those whose talent could be used he employed them; those with no means of support he provided with provisions; for women he arranged marriages and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a hundred families of scholars exiled to the south who could not return north, and of those tainted by criminal connections—whoever had usable talent he put to use; whoever lacked support he supplied with provisions; for women he arranged marriages and saw them properly settled.

sentences.zh: 蕃舶泊步有下碇稅，始至有閱貨宴，所餉犀琲，下及仆隸，戣禁絕，無所求索。

translations.literal: When foreign ships anchored there was an anchorage tax; on first arrival there was a banquet to inspect goods. The gifts of rhinoceros horn and beads extended down even to servants; Mo prohibited all of this and sought nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign ships paid anchorage dues, and on arrival there were banquets to inspect cargo, with gifts of rhinoceros horn and beads extending even to servants and attendants. Mo banned all such practices and accepted nothing.

sentences.zh: 舊制，海商死者，官籍其資，滿三月無妻子詣府，則沒入。

translations.literal: By old regulation, when maritime merchants died, the government registered their assets; if after three full months no wife or children came to the prefectural office, the property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules, when overseas merchants died the government registered their property; if after three months no wife or children came to claim it at the prefectural office, it was forfeited.

sentences.zh: 戣以海道歲一往復，茍有驗者不為限，悉推與。

translations.literal: Mo held that because the sea route had but one round trip per year, as long as there was proof there should be no limit, and he fully restored everything to them.
translations.idiomatic: Reasoning that the sea route allowed only one round trip per year, Mo held that as long as claimants could furnish proof, the time limit should not apply, and he returned everything in full.

sentences.zh: 自貞元中，黃洞諸蠻叛，久不平。

translations.literal: Since the Zhenyuan era the various tribes of Huangdong had rebelled and long remained unpacified.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhenyuan era (785–804) the Huangdong tribes had repeatedly rebelled and remained unrested for years.

sentences.zh: 容、桂二管利虜掠，幸有功，乃請合兵討之。

translations.literal: The two circuits of Rong and Gui profited from captive-taking and plunder; hoping for merit they requested combined forces to campaign against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Rong and Gui circuits profited from raiding and captives and, hoping for glory, requested a joint military campaign against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 戣固言不可，帝不聽，大發江、湖兵，會二管入討。

translations.literal: Mo firmly stated it could not be done; the emperor would not listen and massively mobilized troops from the Jiang and Hu regions, joining the two circuits in the punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Mo adamantly opposed the plan, but the emperor overruled him and mustered large forces from the Jiang and Hu regions for a joint expedition with the two circuits.

sentences.zh: 士被瘴毒死者不勝計，安南乘之，殺都護李象古，而桂管裴行立、容管陽旻皆無功，憂死；

translations.literal: Soldiers who died from malarial poison were beyond counting; Annan seized the opportunity and killed Protector-General Li Xianggu. Both Pei Xingli of the Gui circuit and Yang Min of the Rong circuit achieved nothing and died of grief;
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers died of malarial fevers beyond all count. Annan took advantage of the turmoil and killed Protector-General Li Xianggu. Pei Xingli of Gui circuit and Yang Min of Rong circuit both accomplished nothing and died of distress;

sentences.zh: 獨戣不邀一旦功，交、廣晏然大治。

translations.literal: Mo alone did not grasp at sudden glory; Jiao and Guang were peacefully and greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Mo alone refrained from chasing quick victories, and the Jiao and Guang regions were governed in settled peace.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，以吏部侍郎召，改右散騎常侍，還為左丞，以老自乞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong acceded, Mo was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, changed to Right Regular Attendant of Casual Riders, then returned as Left Assistant Director, and on account of age requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Mo was recalled as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Guard, then returned as Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, and on grounds of age asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 雅善韓愈，謂曰：「公尚壯，上三留，何去之果？」

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Han Yu, who said to him: "Sir, you are still vigorous; the sovereign thrice tried to keep you—why leave so resolutely?
translations.idiomatic: He and Han Yu were close friends. Han Yu said to him: "You are still vigorous, and the emperor tried three times to keep you—why resign so decisively?

sentences.zh: 戣曰：「吾豈要君者？

translations.literal: Mo said: "Do you think I am begging favor from you?
translations.idiomatic: Mo said: "Do you think I am currying favor with you?

sentences.zh: 吾年，一宜去；

translations.literal: My years give one reason to leave;
translations.idiomatic: My age is one reason I should go;

sentences.zh: 吾為左丞，不能進退郎官，二宜去。」

translations.literal: I serve as Left Assistant Director yet cannot appoint or dismiss court gentlemen— a second reason to leave."
translations.idiomatic: As Left Assistant Director I cannot appoint or dismiss court officials—that is a second reason."

sentences.zh: 愈曰：「公無留資，何恃而歸？」

translations.literal: Han Yu said: "Sir, you have no reserve funds— on what do you rely in returning home?"
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu said: "You have no savings. What will you live on when you go home?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾負二宜去，尚奚顧子言？」

translations.literal: He said: "I bear these two reasons to leave— why should I still heed your words?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "I already have two good reasons to leave— why should I worry about what you say?"

sentences.zh: 愈嗟嘆，即上疏言：「臣與戣同在南省，數與戣相見，其為人守節清苦，論議正平。

translations.literal: Han Yu sighed in admiration and immediately submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant and Mo both served in the southern offices; I have often seen Mo. In person he maintains integrity and lives plainly; in debate he is upright and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu sighed deeply and at once submitted a memorial: "I have served with Mo in the southern offices and know him well. He lives with integrity and austerity, and his judgments are fair and principled.

sentences.zh: 年七十，筋力耳目未衰，憂國忘家，用意至到。

translations.literal: Though seventy years old, his sinews, strength, hearing, and sight are not yet diminished; he grieves for the state and forgets his household; his purpose is thoroughly earnest.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy his body and senses are still strong, he cherishes the nation above his own family, and his devotion is complete.

sentences.zh: 如戣輩，在朝不過三數人，陛下不宜茍順其求，不留自助也。

translations.literal: Men like Mo number no more than three or four in court; Your Majesty ought not casually grant his request and fail to keep him to aid yourself.
translations.idiomatic: There are scarcely three or four men like Mo left at court. Your Majesty should not lightly grant his request and lose his counsel.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：大夫七十致事，若不得謝，則賜之幾杖安車，不必七十盡許致事。

translations.literal: The Rites say: at seventy a grandee retires from office; if he may not be released, then he is granted a staff and a comfortable carriage—one need not permit all seventy-year-olds to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites states that at seventy a minister may retire, but if the emperor needs him, he may gift him a staff and a comfortable carriage—the rule does not require that every seventy-year-old be allowed to resign.

sentences.zh: 今戣據禮求退，陛下若不聽許，亦無傷義，而有貪賢之美。」

translations.literal: Now Mo requests retirement according to the Rites; if Your Majesty does not approve, this also does not harm propriety but shows the beauty of coveting worthy men."
translations.idiomatic: Mo is asking to retire as the Rites permit; if Your Majesty refuses, no principle is violated—and you gain the reputation of valuing talent."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made no reply.

sentences.zh: 以禮部尚書致仕，歲致羊酒如漢征士禮。

translations.literal: He retired as Minister of Rites; each year wine and mutton were sent as in the Han rite for summoning scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the title Minister of Rites, and each year received gifts of wine and mutton as under the Han dynasty rite for retired scholars.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部尚書，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Minister of War; his posthumous epithet was Zhen (Upright).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of War and given the posthumous name Upright.

sentences.zh: 子 遵孺

translations.literal: Son: Zunru
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zunru

sentences.zh: 子遵孺，溫裕，仕為天平節度使。

translations.literal: His son Zunru, styled Wenyu, served as Military Governor of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zunru, styled Wenyu, served as military governor of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 遵孺子緯。

translations.literal: Zunru's son Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zunru's son was Wei.

sentences.zh: 遵孺子 緯

translations.literal: Zunru's son: Wei
translations.idiomatic: Son of Zunru: Wei

sentences.zh: 緯，字化文，少孤，依諸父。

translations.literal: Wei, courtesy name Huawen, lost his father young and relied on his uncles.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, styled Huawen, was orphaned young and was raised by his uncles.

sentences.zh: 多與有名者遊，才譽蚤成。

translations.literal: He often associated with famous men; his talent and reputation matured early.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled widely in the circles of distinguished men and won an early reputation for talent.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，東川崔慎由表置幕府。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; Cui Shenyou of Dongchuan recommended him for a staff appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, and Cui Shenyou of Dongchuan had him placed on his staff.

sentences.zh: 從崔鉉淮南，復從慎由守河中，再遷觀察判官。

translations.literal: He followed Cui Xuan to Huainan, then again followed Shenyou in governing Hezhong; after two promotions he became Administrative Aide to the Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Cui Xuan to Huainan, then served again under Shenyou as prefect of Hezhong, and after two promotions became administrative aide to a military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 宰相楊收薦以長安尉直弘文館。

translations.literal: The chancellor Yang Shou recommended him as assistant magistrate of Chang'an and concurrently as erudite of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Counselor Yang Shou recommended him for the post of assistant magistrate of Chang'an and a concurrent appointment as erudite of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史，進禮部員外郎、兼集賢直學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor, promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, and concurrently made Erudite of the Jixian Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the censorate, promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, and given a concurrent appointment as erudite of the Jixian Academy.

sentences.zh: 母喪解。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he resigned office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned from office upon his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 還為右司員外郎。

translations.literal: Upon returning he served as Vice Director of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from mourning he was appointed Vice Director of the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 趙隱言其才，拜翰林學士，俄知制誥。

translations.literal: Zhao Yin spoke of his talent; he was appointed Hanlin Academician and soon put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yin praised his ability, and he was appointed Hanlin Academician; before long he was placed in charge of drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 頻遷戶部侍郎，擢御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and then advanced to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he rose to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, then was elevated to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 緯方雅，疾惡若仇，中外聞風，未繩輒肅。

translations.literal: Wei was upright and refined; he hated evil as if it were a personal enemy; inside and outside the court, upon hearing of him people were awed, and before the rope was applied they were already subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was dignified and unbending; he loathed wickedness with the fervor of a vendetta. His reputation struck fear through court and countryside alike—men fell into line before he ever raised a hand against them.

sentences.zh: 三遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After three further promotions he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 權要私謁至盈幾，一不省，當路不悅，改太常卿。

translations.literal: Powerful men sent private callers until his desk overflowed; he received not one of them; those in power were displeased, and he was reassigned as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Men of influence sent private visitors until his desk was piled high with calling cards, yet he refused every one of them. Those in power took offense, and he was transferred to the post of Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 從僖宗西到蜀，以刑部尚書判戶部。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xizong west to Shu and, with the title Minister of Justice, concurrently handled the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xizong westward into Shu, serving as Minister of Justice with concurrent responsibility for the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 蕭遘雅不喜，坐調度不給，改太子少保。

translations.literal: Xiao You had long disliked him; on the charge of failing to supply provisions he was reassigned as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao You had long borne him ill will. On the charge that he had failed to supply provisions, Wei was demoted to Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 及帝避朱玫，次陳倉，惟黃門衛士數百扈乘輿。

translations.literal: When the emperor fled Zhu Mei and halted at Chencang, only a few hundred attendants of the Yellow Gate guard escorted the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled Zhu Mei and halted at Chencang, only a few hundred attendants of the Yellow Gate guard remained to escort the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 詔拜緯御史大夫，令趣百官至行在。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Wei Censor-in-Chief and ordered him to hasten the hundred officials to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Wei Censor-in-Chief and charged him with hurrying the assembled officials to the emperor's mobile court.

sentences.zh: 時群臣露次盩厔，為盜剽脅，衣囊略盡。

translations.literal: At the time the assembled ministers camped in the open at Zhouzhi; they were robbed and plundered by bandits, and their clothing and bags were nearly emptied.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the assembled ministers were encamped in the open at Zhouzhi; bandits robbed and plundered them until their clothing and baggage were nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 緯謁宰相，欲有所論，遘與裴澈怨田令孜，不欲行，辭不見。

translations.literal: Wei paid a visit to the chancellor, wishing to discuss something; You and Pei Che bore grudges against Tian Lingzi and did not wish to go; they declined and refused to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei called on the chancellor, intending to discuss the matter, but You and Pei Che, who both resented Tian Lingzi, did not wish to go and declined to receive him.

sentences.zh: 緯召御史曰：「吾等身被恩，誼不辭難，今詔群臣皆不至，夫與人布衣遊，猶緩急相恤，況於君乎？」

translations.literal: Wei summoned the censors and said: "We ourselves have received grace; in duty we cannot shrink from hardship. Now the edict has gone out and yet the assembled ministers have not come. Even when one travels with a man in plain cloth, in crisis one still aids one another—how much more so toward one's sovereign?
translations.idiomatic: Wei summoned the censors and said: "We have all received the emperor's grace; in duty we cannot refuse hardship. The edict has gone out, yet the assembled ministers have not come. Even when one travels with a man in common dress, one still helps him in time of need—how much more so toward one's sovereign?

sentences.zh: 且泣下。

translations.literal: As he spoke, he wept.
translations.idiomatic: As he spoke, tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 御史亦辭方寇奪，丐衣食，請辦一日費而行。

translations.literal: The censors also pleaded that bandits had just stripped them; they begged for clothes and food and asked to gather expenses for one day's journey before setting out.
translations.idiomatic: The censors also pleaded that bandits had just robbed them bare; they begged for clothing and food and asked to scrape together enough for one day's travel before departing.

sentences.zh: 緯曰：「吾妻疾，旦暮盡，丈夫豈以家事後國事乎？

translations.literal: Wei said: "My wife is ill and near death. Should a man put household matters before affairs of state?
translations.idiomatic: Wei said: "My wife lies ill and is near death. Should a man put family affairs ahead of the affairs of state?

sentences.zh: 公善自謀，吾行決矣。」

translations.literal: See to your own interests as you will; my departure is decided.
translations.idiomatic: Look to your own affairs as you see fit—I am resolved to go.

sentences.zh: 往見李昌符曰：「詔書再至，而群臣顧未行。

translations.literal: He went to see Li Changfu and said: "The edict has come twice, yet the assembled ministers still hold back from going.
translations.idiomatic: He went to see Li Changfu and said: "The edict has arrived twice, yet the assembled ministers still hesitate to go.

sentences.zh: 仆，大夫也，不敢後。

translations.literal: I, though a grandee, dare not lag behind.
translations.idiomatic: I, your humble servant, though only a grandee, dare not fall behind.

sentences.zh: 願假兵護送天子所。」

translations.literal: I ask to borrow troops to escort me to the emperor's place."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that you lend me troops to escort me to the emperor's side."

sentences.zh: 昌符具資裝送之。

translations.literal: Changfu fully provisioned him and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Changfu fully outfitted him with supplies and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 既及行在，緯策玫必反，建言關邑厄狹，不足駐六師，請幸梁州。

translations.literal: Once he reached the mobile court, Wei calculated that Mei would surely rebel; he advised that the passes and narrow territory could not hold the imperial army and requested that the emperor proceed to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the mobile court, Wei judged that Mei would surely rebel. He urged that the narrow passes could not accommodate the imperial army and asked that the emperor proceed to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 即日去陳倉而玫兵至，微緯言幾不脫。

translations.literal: That very day they left Chencang and Mei's troops arrived; but for Wei's words they would barely have escaped.
translations.idiomatic: They left Chencang that very day, and Mei's troops arrived immediately afterward; but for Wei's counsel they would scarcely have escaped.

sentences.zh: 進拜兵部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War and made Co-Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War and appointed Co-Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 玫平，從帝還，領諸道鹽鐵轉運使，累遷尚書左仆射，賜號「持危啟運保乂功臣」。

translations.literal: After Mei was suppressed, he followed the emperor back, took charge as Commissioner for Salt, Iron, and Transport throughout the circuits, was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and was granted the title "Meritorious Minister Who Upheld Crisis, Initiated Fortune, and Preserved Order."
translations.idiomatic: After Mei was suppressed, he followed the emperor back to the capital, took charge as Commissioner for Salt, Iron, and Transport throughout the circuits, rose to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and was granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Upheld Crisis, Initiated Fortune, and Preserved Order.

sentences.zh: 鐵券恕十死，又賜天興良田、善和裏第各一區，兼京畿營田使。

translations.literal: He was granted an iron certificate forgiving ten capital offenses; he was also given one tract of fine land at Tianxing and one mansion in the Shanhe Ward, and concurrently made Commissioner for Agricultural Colonies in the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: He received an iron certificate forgiving ten capital offenses, was granted one tract of fine land at Tianxing and one mansion in the Shanhe Ward, and was concurrently appointed Commissioner for Agricultural Colonies in the Capital Region.

sentences.zh: 張濬將伐太原，帝不決，以問緯，緯助濬請。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jun was about to campaign against Taiyuan, the emperor was undecided and consulted Wei; Wei supported Jun's request.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun was preparing to campaign against Taiyuan, the emperor could not decide and asked Wei, who supported Jun's request.

sentences.zh: 既濬敗，坐傅會，出為荊南節度使，俄貶均州刺史。

translations.literal: After Jun was defeated, Wei was implicated for conspiring with him and was sent out as military commissioner of Jingnan; soon he was demoted to prefect of Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Jun's defeat, Wei was punished for having sided with him and was sent out as military commissioner of Jingnan; before long he was demoted to prefect of Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二人皆密結朱全忠，全忠為請，詔聽所便，乃屏居華陰。

translations.literal: Both men secretly allied themselves with Zhu Quanzhong; Quanzhong petitioned on their behalf; an edict allowed them to live where they pleased, and they then retired to Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Both men secretly allied themselves with Zhu Quanzhong. Quanzhong petitioned on their behalf, and an edict permitted them to live where they chose; they then withdrew to Huayin.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞入殺韋昭度，帝惡大臣朋比，與藩臣交，更召緯入朝，再擢吏部尚書，以司空、門下侍郎復輔政。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen entered and killed Wei Zhaodu; the emperor was displeased that grand ministers banded together and consorted with frontier lords; Wei was again summoned to court, once more elevated to Minister of Personnel, and with the titles of Minister of Works and Vice Director of the Chancellery he again assisted in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen entered the capital and killed Wei Zhaodu. The emperor was angered that grand ministers were forming factions and consorting with frontier lords. Wei was summoned back to court, again promoted to Minister of Personnel, and with the titles of Minister of Works and Vice Director of the Chancellery he once more joined the government.

sentences.zh: 使者敦勸，力疾到京師，見帝嗚咽流涕，自陳衰疾不任事，乞歸田裏。

translations.literal: The emissaries urged him earnestly; forcing himself despite illness he reached the capital; seeing the emperor he sobbed and wept, declaring himself old and ill and unfit for office, and begged to return to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: The emissaries pressed him earnestly. Forcing himself onward despite illness, he reached the capital; when he saw the emperor he sobbed and wept, declaring himself aged and infirm and unfit for office, and begged to retire to his fields.

sentences.zh: 帝動容，詔使者送緯至堂視事。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply moved and ordered the emissaries to escort Wei to the hall of office so he could attend to business.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and ordered the emissaries to escort Wei to the hall of office so that he might take up his duties.

sentences.zh: 會天子出次石門，從至莎城，以病還都。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven went out and halted at Shimen, he followed as far as Shacheng; then, owing to illness, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went out and halted at Shimen, Wei followed as far as Shacheng, then returned to the capital on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 家人召醫視，緯曰：「天下方亂，何久求生？」

translations.literal: His family summoned a doctor to attend him; Wei said: "The empire is in turmoil—why cling to life?
translations.idiomatic: His family summoned a physician, but Wei said: "The empire is in turmoil—why should I cling to life?

sentences.zh: 不肯服藥，卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He refused to take medicine and died; posthumously he was given the title of Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to take medicine and died. Posthumously he was granted the title Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 從子 戡

translations.literal: Nephew: Kan
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Kan

sentences.zh: 戡，字勝始，進士及第，補修武尉，以大理評事佐昭義李長榮節度府。

translations.literal: Kan, courtesy name Shengshi, passed the jinshi examination; he was appointed assistant magistrate of Xiuwu; as reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review he served on the staff of Li Changrong, military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Kan, styled Shengshi, passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Xiuwu. As a reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review he served on the staff of Li Changrong, military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 長榮死，盧從史自別將代之，留署掌書記。

translations.literal: When Changrong died, Lu Congshi as deputy commander replaced him and kept Kan on staff as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Changrong died, Lu Congshi replaced him from the rank of deputy commander and retained Kan on staff as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 從史稍得誌，益驕，與王承宗、田緒陰相結，欲久連兵以固其位。

translations.literal: As Congshi gradually got his way he grew more arrogant; he secretly allied with Wang Chengzong and Tian Xu, intending to prolong hostilities in order to secure his position.
translations.idiomatic: As Congshi gradually had his way he grew ever more arrogant. He secretly allied with Wang Chengzong and Tian Xu, intending to keep the armies fighting so as to secure his own position.

sentences.zh: 戡始陰爭不從，則於會肆言以折之，從史始若受其言，後偃蹇不軌，戡遂以疾歸洛陽。

translations.literal: At first Kan privately remonstrated, and when not obeyed he would speak openly at gatherings to refute him; Congshi at first seemed to accept his words, but later became insolently unruly; Kan then pleaded illness and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first Kan remonstrated in private, and when Congshi would not listen he spoke openly at gatherings to refute him. Congshi at first seemed to heed his words, but later grew insolent and unruly, and Kan then pleaded illness and returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李吉甫鎮揚州，表置幕府，戡未應。

translations.literal: Before long Li Jifu governed Yangzhou and petitioned to place him on his staff; Kan did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Jifu took charge at Yangzhou and petitioned to have Kan placed on his staff, but Kan did not respond.

sentences.zh: 從史曰：「是欲舍我而從人邪？」

translations.literal: Congshi said: "Does he mean to abandon me and follow someone else?
translations.idiomatic: Congshi said: "Does he mean to abandon me and go serve someone else?

sentences.zh: 即誣以事，奏三上，詔以衛尉丞分司東都。

translations.literal: He immediately fabricated charges and memorialized three times; an edict appointed Kan Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately fabricated charges against him and submitted memorials three times. An edict appointed Kan Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia with duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 自貞元後，帥鎮劾奏僚佐，不驗輒斥。

translations.literal: Since the Zhenyuan era, military commissioners had impeached staff members, and without verification they were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhenyuan era, military commissioners who impeached their staff members had them dismissed without investigation.

sentences.zh: 至是，給事中呂元膺執不可。

translations.literal: On this occasion Supervising Secretary Lü Yuanying held that it could not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion Supervising Secretary Lü Yuanying objected that this could not be permitted.

sentences.zh: 憲宗遣使諭曰：「朕非不知戡，行用之矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong sent an emissary to explain: "It is not that We do not know Kan—we are about to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong sent an emissary to explain: "It is not that We do not recognize Kan's worth—we intend to employ him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 從史敗，追贈司勛員外郎。

translations.literal: When Congshi was defeated, Kan was posthumously given the title Vice Director of the Ministry of Honors.
translations.idiomatic: When Congshi was defeated, Kan was posthumously granted the title Vice Director of the Ministry of Honors.

sentences.zh: 從子 戢

translations.literal: Nephew: Ji
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Ji

sentences.zh: 戢，字方舉。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Fangju.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, styled Fangju.

sentences.zh: 初，父死難，詔與一子官，補修武尉，不受，以讓其兄戡。

translations.literal: Initially, when his father died in the line of duty, an edict granted an office to one son; he was appointed assistant magistrate of Xiuwu but declined, yielding it to his elder brother Kan.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died in the line of duty, an edict granted an office to one son. Ji was appointed assistant magistrate of Xiuwu but declined, yielding the post to his elder brother Kan.

sentences.zh: 擢明經，書判高等，為校書郎、陽翟尉，累遷殿中侍御史，分司東都。

translations.literal: He passed the mingjing examination and ranked high in the document-judgment test; he served as collator and magistrate of Yangdi; he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Censor with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the mingjing examination and ranked high in the document-judgment test. He served as collator and magistrate of Yangdi, then rose to Palace Censor with duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 昭義判官徐玫，故嘗助盧從史為跋扈者，從史敗，孟元陽代，欲復用之。

translations.literal: Xu Mei, administrative aide of Zhaoyi, had previously helped Lu Congshi in his overbearing conduct; after Congshi's defeat, when Meng Yuanyang replaced him, he wished to employ Mei again.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mei, an administrative aide of Zhaoyi, had once helped Lu Congshi in his overbearing conduct. After Congshi's defeat, when Meng Yuanyang replaced him, he wished to employ Mei again.

sentences.zh: 戢移書昭義前系玫，乃上列其狀。

translations.literal: Ji sent a letter to Zhaoyi ordering Mei detained beforehand, then submitted a memorial detailing his offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Ji sent a letter to Zhaoyi ordering Mei detained in advance, then submitted a memorial detailing his offenses.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，流玫播州。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered and banished Mei to Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and banished Mei to Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 轉侍御史、庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regular censor and Vice Director of the Treasury Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regular censor and Vice Director of the Treasury Bureau.

sentences.zh: 始，朱泚以彭偃為中書舍人，偃子充符得不死，辟鄜坊府。

translations.literal: Initially Zhu Ci made Peng Yan a Drafting Secretary; Yan's son Chongfu escaped death and was recruited to the Bin-Fang headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhu Ci had made Peng Yan a Drafting Secretary. Yan's son Chongfu escaped execution and was recruited to the Bin-Fang headquarters.

sentences.zh: 或薦其能，召還京師。

translations.literal: Someone recommended his ability and he was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Someone recommended his talents, and he was summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 戢謂京兆尹裴武曰：「泚所下詔令皆偃為之，悖逆子不鳥竄獸伏，乃幹譽求進乎？

translations.literal: Ji said to Pei Wu, Intendant of the Capital: "The edicts Zhu Ci issued were all composed by Yan—should this traitor's son, instead of hiding like a bird in its nest or a beast in its burrow, now seek reputation and advancement?
translations.idiomatic: Ji said to Pei Wu, Intendant of the Capital: "Every edict Zhu Ci issued was composed by Yan. Should this traitor's son, instead of hiding like a bird in its nest or a beast in its lair, now seek fame and advancement?

sentences.zh: 子盍效季孫行父逐莒仆以勉事君者？」

translations.literal: Would you not do as Jisun Xingfu drove out Ju Pu, to encourage those who serve their lord?
translations.idiomatic: Why not follow Jisun Xingfu's example in driving out Ju Pu, to encourage those who serve their sovereign?

sentences.zh: 武即逐出充符。

translations.literal: Wu immediately expelled Chongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu immediately expelled Chongfu.

sentences.zh: 拜京兆少尹，再遷為湖南觀察使，召授右散騎常侍、京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Intendant of the Capital; after two promotions he became Military Commissioner of Hunan; summoned and given the title Right Regular Attendant and Intendant of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Intendant of the Capital, then after two promotions became Military Commissioner of Hunan. Summoned back, he was given the titles Right Regular Attendant and Intendant of the Capital.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，文宗憂甚，戢躬祠曲江池，一夕大澍，帝悅，詔兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: During a year of drought Emperor Wenzong was deeply troubled; Ji personally offered sacrifice at Qujiang Pool; overnight there fell a great downpour; the emperor was pleased and ordered him to serve concurrently as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During a year of drought Emperor Wenzong was deeply troubled. Ji personally offered sacrifice at Qujiang Pool, and overnight a great rain fell. The emperor was delighted and ordered him to serve concurrently as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given the title Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died. Posthumously he was granted the title Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 子 溫業

translations.literal: Son: Wenye
translations.idiomatic: Son: Wenye

sentences.zh: 子溫業，字遜誌，擢進士第。

translations.literal: His son Wenye, courtesy name Xunzhi, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenye, styled Xunzhi, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 大中時，為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Dazhong era he served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong era he served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 求外遷，宰相白敏中顧同列曰：「吾等可少警，孔吏部不樂居朝矣。」

translations.literal: He sought transfer outside the capital; the chancellor Bai Minzhong turned to his colleagues and said: "We ought to take warning—Vice Minister Kong no longer wishes to remain at court.
translations.idiomatic: He sought a transfer out of the capital. Chancellor Bai Minzhong turned to his colleagues and said: "We ought to take warning—Vice Minister Kong no longer wishes to remain at court.

sentences.zh: 後為太子賓客。

translations.literal: Later he served as Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 穆寧，懷州河內人。

translations.literal: Mu Ning was a native of Henei in Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Ning was a native of Henei in Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 父元休，有名開元間，獻書天子，擢偃師丞，世以儒聞。

translations.literal: His father Yuanxiu was famous during the Kaiyuan era; he presented books to the Son of Heaven and was promoted to assistant magistrate of Yanshi; the family was renowned as scholars.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanxiu won renown during the Kaiyuan era. He presented books to the emperor and was promoted to assistant magistrate of Yanshi; the family was known for generations as scholars.

sentences.zh: 寧剛正，氣節自任。

translations.literal: Ning was sternly upright and took moral resolve as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was sternly upright and held himself to the highest standards of integrity.

sentences.zh: 以明經調鹽山尉。

translations.literal: Through the mingjing examination he was assigned as magistrate of Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the mingjing examination, he was assigned as magistrate of Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，署劉道玄為景城守，寧募兵斬之，檄州縣並力捍賊。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he appointed Liu Daoxuan prefect of Jingcheng; Ning raised troops, beheaded him, and issued a proclamation calling on prefectures and counties to join forces in resisting the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he appointed Liu Daoxuan prefect of Jingcheng. Ning raised troops, beheaded him, and issued a proclamation calling on prefectures and counties to join forces against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 史思明略境，郡守召寧攝東光令禦之。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming overran the territory, the prefect summoned Ning to act as magistrate of Dongguang to defend against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming overran the region, the prefect summoned Ning to serve as acting magistrate of Dongguang and defend against him.

sentences.zh: 賊遣使誘寧，寧斬以徇，郡守恐怒賊令致死，即奪其兵，罷所攝。

translations.literal: The rebels sent envoys to entice Ning; Ning beheaded them as a public warning; the prefect feared angering the rebels would bring death upon them, so he stripped Ning of his troops and removed him from his acting post.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent envoys to win Ning over; Ning beheaded them as a public warning. The prefect feared that provoking the rebels would bring ruin upon them, so he stripped Ning of his troops and removed him from his acting post.

sentences.zh: 始，寧過平原，見顏真卿，嘗商賊必反。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ning passed through Pingyuan and met Yan Zhenqing, they had discussed that the rebels would surely turn against the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ning passed through Pingyuan and met Yan Zhenqing, they had discussed how the rebels would surely turn against the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 及是，聞真卿拒祿山，即遺真卿書曰：「夫子為衛君乎？」

translations.literal: At this time, hearing that Zhenqing was resisting Lushan, he immediately sent Zhenqing a letter saying: "Will you, Master, serve as Wei's minister did?
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture, hearing that Zhenqing was resisting Lushan, he immediately sent him a letter saying: "Master, will you serve your sovereign as you ought?

sentences.zh: 真卿喜，署寧河北采訪支使。

translations.literal: Zhenqing was delighted and appointed Ning Branch Commissioner of the Hebei Investigation Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing was delighted and appointed Ning Branch Commissioner of the Hebei Investigation Circuit.

sentences.zh: 寧以息屬其母弟曰：「茍不乏嗣，足矣！」

translations.literal: Ning entrusted his son to his younger brother by the same mother, saying: "If only the line is not cut off, that is enough!
translations.idiomatic: Ning entrusted his son to his younger brother by the same mother, saying: "So long as the line is not cut off, that is enough!

sentences.zh: 即馳謁真卿曰：「先人有嗣矣，我可從公死。」

translations.literal: He then galloped to pay his respects to Zhenqing and said: "My forebear now has an heir; I may follow you to the death."
translations.idiomatic: He then rode at once to see Zhenqing and said: "My father now has an heir; I may follow you to the death."

sentences.zh: 既而賊攻平原，寧勸固守，真卿不從，夜亡過河，見肅宗行在。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels attacked Pingyuan; Ning urged holding firm, but Zhenqing would not agree; by night he fled across the river and went to Emperor Suzong's mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels attacked Pingyuan. Ning urged holding the city, but Zhenqing would not agree. By night he fled across the river and went to Emperor Suzong's mobile court.

sentences.zh: 帝問狀，真卿對：「不用穆寧言，故至此。」

translations.literal: The emperor inquired into the situation; Zhenqing replied: "Because I did not follow Mu Ning's advice, I have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inquired into the situation. Zhenqing replied: "Because I did not heed Mu Ning's counsel, I have come to this pass.

sentences.zh: 帝異之，馳驛召寧，將以諫議大夫任之。

translations.literal: The emperor was impressed; he dispatched relay horses to summon Ning and intended to appoint him Remonstrance and Advice Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed. He dispatched relay horses to summon Ning and intended to appoint him Remonstrance and Advice Grandee.

sentences.zh: 會真卿以直忤旨，寧亦罷。

translations.literal: Just then Zhenqing, for his bluntness, offended the emperor's intent; Ning was dismissed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Zhenqing, for his bluntness, gave offense to the emperor, and Ning was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 上元初，為殿中侍御史，佐鹽鐵轉運，住埇橋。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shangyuan era he served as Palace Censor, assisting in salt-and-iron transport administration, stationed at Yongqiao.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shangyuan era he served as Palace Censor, assisting in salt-and-iron transport administration, and was stationed at Yongqiao.

sentences.zh: 李光弼屯徐州，餉不至，檄取資糧，寧不與。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi was encamped at Xuzhou; supplies did not arrive; he issued an order requisitioning provisions; Ning refused to release them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi was encamped at Xuzhou, but supplies did not arrive. He issued an order requisitioning provisions, and Ning refused to release them.

sentences.zh: 光弼怒，召寧欲殺之。

translations.literal: Guangbi was furious and summoned Ning intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi was furious and summoned Ning, intending to kill him.

sentences.zh: 或勸寧去，寧曰：「避之失守，亂自我始，何所逃罪乎？」

translations.literal: Someone urged Ning to flee; Ning said: "To flee would be to abandon my post; disorder would begin with me—where could I escape blame?
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Ning to flee, but Ning said: "To flee would be to abandon my post. Disorder would begin with me—where could I escape blame?

sentences.zh: 即往見光弼。

translations.literal: He went at once to see Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: He went at once to see Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「吾師眾數萬，為天子討賊，食乏則人散，君閉廩不救，欲潰吾兵耶？」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "My army numbers tens of thousands, campaigning for the Son of Heaven against rebels—if food runs out the men will scatter; you lock the granaries and refuse aid—do you wish to break my army?
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said: "My army numbers in the tens of thousands, campaigning for the emperor against rebels. If food runs out the men will scatter. You lock the granaries and refuse aid—do you wish to break my army?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「命寧主糧者，敕也，公可以檄取乎？

translations.literal: He replied: "The one who ordered Ning to manage provisions was the imperial edict—can you requisition them by military dispatch alone?
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "The one who ordered me to manage provisions was the imperial edict. Can you requisition them by military dispatch alone?

sentences.zh: 今公求糧，而寧專饋；

translations.literal: If you now demand grain and Ning alone dispenses it,
translations.idiomatic: If you now demand grain and I alone dispense it,

sentences.zh: 寧有求兵，而公亦專與乎？」

translations.literal: if Ning should demand troops, would you also dispense them on your sole authority?"
translations.idiomatic: if I should demand troops, would you also dispense them on your sole authority?"

sentences.zh: 光弼執其手謝曰：「吾固知不可，聊與君議耳。」

translations.literal: Guangbi took his hand and apologized: "I knew all along it could not be done—I was only discussing it with you."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi took his hand and apologized: "I knew all along it could not be done—I was only sounding you out."

sentences.zh: 時重其能守官。

translations.literal: At the time people esteemed his ability to hold to his office.
translations.idiomatic: At the time people greatly admired his steadfastness in office.

sentences.zh: 累遷鄂嶽沔都團練及租庸鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Overall Training Commissioner of E, Yue, and Mian, and Commissioner for Tax Corvée, Salt, and Iron Transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Overall Training Commissioner of E, Yue, and Mian, and Commissioner for Tax Corvée, Salt, and Iron Transport.

sentences.zh: 當是時，河漕不通，自漢、沔徑商山以入京師。

translations.literal: At that time the canal route was impassable; freight entered the capital by way of Han and Mian, taking the route through Shang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the canal transport route was blocked; goods reached the capital only by way of Han and Mian, passing through Shang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 淮西節度使李忠臣不奉法，設戍邏以征商賈，又縱兵剽行人，道路幾絕。

translations.literal: The Huai-Xi military governor Li Zhongchen did not observe the law; he established frontier posts to levy exactions on merchants, and also let his troops plunder travelers—the roads were nearly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen, military governor of Huai-Xi, flouted the law. He set up frontier posts to levy exactions on merchants and let his soldiers pillage travelers, so that the roads were all but closed.

sentences.zh: 與寧夾淮為治，憚寧威，掠劫為衰，漕賈得通。

translations.literal: Governing on opposite banks of the Huai alongside Ning, he feared Ning's authority; plunder and robbery declined, and canal transport and commerce were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Governing on opposite banks of the Huai alongside Ning, he feared Ning's authority. Predation waned, and canal transport and merchants could move freely again.

sentences.zh: 坐杖死沔州別駕，貶平集尉。

translations.literal: For beating the Vice-Prefect of Mian to death, he was demoted to Registrar of Pingji.
translations.idiomatic: For beating the vice-prefect of Mian Prefecture to death, he was demoted to registrar of Pingji.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，起為監察御史，三遷檢校秘書少監，兼和州刺史，治有狀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali reign, he was recalled to serve as Supervising Censor; after three promotions he became Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Prefect of He Prefecture, and his governance showed merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dali reign he was recalled to serve as supervising censor. After three promotions he became acting vice director of the Secretariat and concurrently prefect of He Prefecture, and his administration showed clear merit.

sentences.zh: 後刺史疾之，以天寶舊版校見戶，妄劾寧多逋亡，貶泉州司戶參軍事。

translations.literal: Later the prefect resented him; using the Tianbao-era household register to compare registered households, he falsely impeached Ning for numerous absconded taxpayers and had him demoted to Revenue Section Administrator of Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later the prefect took a dislike to him. Using the Tianbao-era household register to check registered households, he falsely impeached Ning for widespread tax evasion and had him demoted to revenue section administrator of Quan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子贊訴其枉，三年始得通。

translations.literal: His son Zan appealed the injustice; only after three years did the appeal get through.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zan appealed the injustice, but only after three years did the petition reach the court.

sentences.zh: 詔御史覆視，實增戶數倍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered censors to reinvestigate; the households had in fact increased several times over.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered censors to reinvestigate, and they found that the number of households had in fact increased several times over.

sentences.zh: 召入拜太子右諭德。

translations.literal: He was summoned to court and appointed Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed right mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 寧性不能事權右，毅然寡合，執政者惡之，雖直其誣，猶置散位。

translations.literal: Ning by nature could not defer to the powerful; resolute and little inclined to compromise, he was hated by those in power; though his false accusation was cleared, he was still given an honorary post without duties.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Ning could not defer to the powerful. Resolute and little inclined to compromise, he was disliked by those in power. Though his false accusation was cleared, he was still given an honorary post without real duties.

sentences.zh: 寧默不樂，唶曰：「時不我容，我不時徇，又可以進乎！」

translations.literal: Ning kept silent and was unhappy, sighing: "The times will not accommodate me; I will not accommodate the times—how then can I advance!
translations.idiomatic: Ning fell silent and unhappy, sighing: "The times will not accommodate me, and I will not bend to the times—how then can I advance!

sentences.zh: 遂移疾，滿百日屢矣，親友強之，輒復一朝。

translations.literal: He then submitted a request for sick leave; when the hundred-day limit was repeatedly reached, friends and kin pressed him, and each time he would attend court for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a request for sick leave. When the hundred-day limit was repeatedly reached, friends and kin pressed him, and each time he would attend court for a single day before resuming his leave.

sentences.zh: 德宗在奉天，奔詣行在，擢秘書少監，改太子右庶子。

translations.literal: When Dezong was at Fengtian, Ning rushed to the mobile court and was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, then changed to Right Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong was at Fengtian, Ning rushed to the mobile court and was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, then reassigned as right vice mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝還京師，乃曰：「可以行吾誌矣！」

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, Ning said: "Now I can act on my resolve!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Ning said: "Now I can act on my resolve!

sentences.zh: 即罷歸東都。

translations.literal: He at once resigned and returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He at once resigned and returned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 以秘書監致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He retired as Director of the Secretariat and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as director of the Secretariat and died.

sentences.zh: 寧居家嚴，事寡姊恭甚。

translations.literal: At home Ning was strict in conduct and treated his elder sister, his only surviving sibling, with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: At home Ning was strict in conduct and treated his elder sister, his only surviving sibling, with great respect.

sentences.zh: 嘗撰家令訓諸子，人一通。

translations.literal: He once composed household instructions for his sons, giving each one a copy.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed household instructions for his sons, giving each one a copy.

sentences.zh: 又戒曰：「君子之事親，養誌為大，吾誌直道而已。

translations.literal: He also admonished them: "In serving one's parents, the greatest form of support is to fulfill their aspirations; my aspiration is nothing but the straight Way.
translations.idiomatic: He also admonished them: "In serving one's parents, the greatest form of support is to fulfill their aspirations. My aspiration is nothing but the straight Way.

sentences.zh: 茍枉而道，三牲五鼎非吾養也。」

translations.literal: If the Way is bent, then even the three sacrificial beasts and the five cauldrons are not support fit for me.
translations.idiomatic: If the Way is bent, then even the finest sacrificial offerings are not support fit for me.

sentences.zh: 疾病不嘗藥，時稱知命。

translations.literal: When ill he would not take medicine; at the time he was praised as one who understood fate.
translations.idiomatic: When ill he would not take medicine; at the time he was praised as one who understood fate.

sentences.zh: 四子：贊、質、員、賞。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Zan, Zhi, Yuan, and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Zan, Zhi, Yuan, and Shang.

sentences.zh: 寧之老，贊為御史中丞，質右補闕，員侍御史，賞監察御史，皆以守道行誼顯。

translations.literal: When Ning was old, Zan was Vice Censor-in-Chief, Zhi was Right Remonstrance Official, Yuan was Attending Censor, and Shang was Supervising Censor—all were distinguished for upholding the Way and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Ning was old, Zan was vice censor-in-chief, Zhi was right remonstrance official, Yuan was attending censor, and Shang was supervising censor—all were distinguished for upholding the Way and integrity.

sentences.zh: 先是，韓休家訓子侄至嚴。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han Xiu had trained his sons and nephews with extreme strictness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Xiu had trained his sons and nephews with extreme strictness.

sentences.zh: 貞元間，言家法者，尚韓、穆二門云。

translations.literal: During the Zhenyuan era, those who spoke of household discipline still looked to the Han and Mu families.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era, those who spoke of household discipline still looked to the Han and Mu families.

sentences.zh: 子 贊

translations.literal: Son: Zan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zan

sentences.zh: 贊，字相明，擢累侍御史，分司東都。

translations.literal: Zan, courtesy name Xiangming, was repeatedly promoted to Attending Censor and served in the Eastern Capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: Zan, styled Xiangming, was repeatedly promoted to attending censor and served in the Eastern Capital branch office.

sentences.zh: 陜虢觀察使盧嶽妻分貲不及妾子，妾訴之。

translations.literal: The Shaan-Guo observation commissioner Lu Yue's wife had not divided the estate equally with the concubine's son; the concubine brought suit.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yue, observation commissioner of Shaan-Guo, had a wife who did not divide the estate equally with the concubine's son; the concubine brought suit.

sentences.zh: 中丞盧佋欲重妾罪，贊不聽。

translations.literal: The Vice Censor-in-Chief Lu Qian wished to impose a heavy penalty on the concubine; Zan would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Lu Qian wished to impose a heavy penalty on the concubine, but Zan would not agree.

sentences.zh: 佋與宰相竇參共誣贊受金，捕送獄。

translations.literal: Qian and the chief minister Dou Can together falsely accused Zan of taking bribes and had him arrested and sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Qian and the chief minister Dou Can together falsely accused Zan of taking bribes and had him arrested and sent to prison.

sentences.zh: 弟賞上冤狀，詔三司覆治，無之，猶出為郴州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shang submitted a petition of injustice; an edict ordered the Three Offices to reinvestigate; nothing was found, yet Zan was still sent out as Prefect of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shang submitted a petition of injustice. An edict ordered the Three Offices to reinvestigate and found no wrongdoing, yet Zan was still sent out as prefect of Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 參敗，召為刑部郎中，對延英，擢御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Can fell from power, Zan was recalled as Director in the Ministry of Justice; facing the emperor in the Yanying Hall, he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Can fell from power, Zan was recalled as director in the Ministry of Justice. Facing the emperor in the Yanying Hall, he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡判度支，屬吏受賕，具獄，欲曲貸吏，贊執不可。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling was in charge of the Department of Public Revenue; a subordinate had taken bribes and the case was complete, but Yanling wished to leniently excuse the official; Zan held firm and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling was in charge of the Department of Public Revenue. A subordinate had taken bribes and the case was complete, but Yanling wished to leniently excuse the official. Zan held firm and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 延齡白贊深文，貶饒州別駕。

translations.literal: Yanling reported that Zan had applied the law with excessive severity, and Zan was demoted to Vice-Prefect of Rao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling reported that Zan had applied the law with excessive severity, and Zan was demoted to vice-prefect of Rao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜州刺史。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Prefect of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed prefect of Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，進宣歙觀察使，卒於官。

translations.literal: When Xianzong acceded, he was promoted to Observation Commissioner of Xuan and She and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong acceded, he was promoted to observation commissioner of Xuan and She and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded the title Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title minister of works.

sentences.zh: 子 質

translations.literal: Son: Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zhi

sentences.zh: 質，性強直，舉賢良方正，條對詳切，頻擢至給事中，政事得失，未嘗不盡言。

translations.literal: Zhi was strong and upright by nature; recommended as Worthy and Upright, his written responses were detailed and incisive; he was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Secretary, and on matters of government gain and loss he never failed to speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was strong and upright by nature. Recommended as Worthy and Upright, his written responses were detailed and incisive. He was repeatedly promoted to supervising secretary, and on matters of government gain and loss he never failed to speak fully.

sentences.zh: 元和時，鹽鐵、轉運諸院擅系囚，笞掠嚴楚，人多死。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhe era, the salt, iron, and transport offices arbitrarily detained prisoners and beat them with severe cruelty; many people died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era, the salt, iron, and transport offices arbitrarily detained prisoners and beat them with severe cruelty, and many people died.

sentences.zh: 質奏請與州縣吏參決，自是不冤。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized requesting that prefectural and county officials participate in deciding cases; from then on there were no wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized requesting that prefectural and county officials participate in deciding cases. From then on there were no wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 後論吐突承璀不宜為將，憲宗不悅，改太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Later he argued that Tutu Chengcui was unfit to be a general; Xianzong was displeased and transferred him to Left Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Later he argued that Tutu Chengcui was unfit to be a general. Xianzong was displeased and transferred him to left vice mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 坐與楊憑善，出為開州刺史，卒。
