translations.literal: For associating with Yang Ping he was sent out as Prefect of Kai Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: For associating with Yang Ping he was sent out as prefect of Kai Prefecture and died.

sentences.zh: 子 員

translations.literal: Son: Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yuan

sentences.zh: 員，字與直，工為文章。

translations.literal: Yuan, courtesy name Yuzhi, was skilled at composing literary works.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, styled Yuzhi, was skilled at composing literary works.

sentences.zh: 杜亞留守東都，置佐其府，蚤卒。

translations.literal: Du Ya was left behind to guard the Eastern Capital and appointed him assistant in his headquarters; he died young.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya was left behind to guard the Eastern Capital and appointed him assistant in his headquarters. He died young.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆和粹，世以珍味目之：贊少俗，然有格，為「酪」；

translations.literal: The brothers were all mild and pure; the age compared them to delicacies: Zan, though somewhat common, yet had character, and was called "curdled milk";
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were all mild and pure; the age compared them to delicacies: Zan, though somewhat common, yet had character, and was called "curdled milk";

sentences.zh: 質美而多入，為「酥」；

translations.literal: Zhi was fine and widely appealing, and was called "butter";
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was fine and widely appealing, and was called "butter";

sentences.zh: 員為「醍醐」；

translations.literal: Yuan was called "ghee";
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was called "ghee";

sentences.zh: 賞為「乳腐」云。

translations.literal: and Shang was called "fermented curd."
translations.idiomatic: and Shang was called "fermented curd."

sentences.zh: 崔邠，字處仁，貝州武城人。

translations.literal: Cui Bin, courtesy name Churen, was a native of Wucheng in Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bin, styled Churen, was a native of Wucheng in Bei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父倕，三世一爨，當時言治家者推其法。

translations.literal: His father Chui maintained one shared kitchen for three generations; at the time those who spoke of household governance praised his methods.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chui maintained one shared kitchen for three generations. At the time those who spoke of household governance praised his methods.

sentences.zh: 至德初，獻賦行在，肅宗異其文，位吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide reign he presented a fu at the mobile court; Suzong was struck by his writing and appointed him Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhide reign he presented a fu at the mobile court. Suzong was struck by his writing and appointed him vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 邠第進士，復擢賢良方正，授渭南尉，遷補闕。

translations.literal: Bin passed the jinshi examination, was again selected as Worthy and Upright, was appointed Registrar of Weinan, and was promoted to Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: Bin passed the jinshi examination, was again selected as Worthy and Upright, was appointed registrar of Weinan, and was promoted to remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 上疏論裴延齡奸，以鯁亮知名。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial denouncing Pei Yanling's treachery and became known for his blunt integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial denouncing Pei Yanling's treachery and became known for his blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 由中書舍人再遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: From Palace Secretariat Drafting Official he was twice promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: From palace secretariat drafting official he was twice promoted to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 性溫裕深密，行己又簡儉，憲宗器之，裴垍亦薦邠材可宰相。

translations.literal: By nature he was warm, generous, and deeply reserved; in personal conduct he was also simple and frugal; Xianzong valued him, and Pei Ji also recommended Bin's talent as suitable for the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was warm, generous, and deeply reserved. In personal conduct he was also simple and frugal. Xianzong valued him, and Pei Ji also recommended Bin's talent as suitable for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 會病，遂不拜。

translations.literal: He happened to fall ill and so was not appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He happened to fall ill and so was not appointed.

sentences.zh: 久乃為太常卿，知吏部尚書銓。

translations.literal: After a long time he became Minister of Rites and oversaw the Ministry of Personnel's selection examinations.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he became minister of rites and oversaw the Ministry of Personnel's selection examinations.

sentences.zh: 故事，太常始視事，大閱四部樂，都人縱觀。

translations.literal: By precedent, when the Minister of Rites first assumed office, the four divisions of music were grandly reviewed and the capital populace was allowed to watch freely.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when the minister of rites first assumed office, the four divisions of music were grandly reviewed and the capital populace was allowed to watch freely.

sentences.zh: 邠自第去帽，親導母輿，公卿見者皆避道，都人榮之。

translations.literal: Bin, from his own residence, removed his cap and personally guided his mother's carriage; officials who saw it all yielded the road, and the people of the capital took pride in it.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, from his own residence, removed his cap and personally guided his mother's carriage. Officials who saw it all yielded the road, and the people of the capital took pride in it.

sentences.zh: 以母憂解，卒於喪，年六十。

translations.literal: He resigned on account of mourning for his mother and died during the mourning period, at the age of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on account of mourning for his mother and died during the mourning period, at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，謚曰文簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded the title Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous name Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title minister of personnel, with the posthumous name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 弟酆、郾、郇、鄯、鄲。

translations.literal: His younger brothers were Feng, Yan, Xun, Shan, and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers were Feng, Yan, Xun, Shan, and Yin.

sentences.zh: 弟 郾

translations.literal: Younger brother: Yan
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Yan

sentences.zh: 郾，字廣略，姿儀偉秀，人望而慕之，然不可狎也。

translations.literal: Yan, courtesy name Guanglue, was tall and handsome in bearing; people gazed at him with admiration, yet he could not be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Guanglue, was tall and handsome in bearing. People gazed at him with admiration, yet he could not be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，補集賢校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部員外郎，下不敢欺，每擬吏，親挾格，褒黜必當，寒遠無留才。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel; subordinates did not dare deceive him; whenever he drafted appointments he personally held the regulations in hand, and promotions and demotions were always appropriate—no talent from humble or distant backgrounds was left unused.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel. Subordinates did not dare deceive him. Whenever he drafted appointments he personally held the regulations in hand, and promotions and demotions were always appropriate—no talent from humble or distant backgrounds was left unused.

sentences.zh: 三遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Remonstrance and Reproof Official.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became remonstrance and reproof official.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，荒於遊畋，內酣蕩，昕曙不能朝。

translations.literal: When Muzong acceded, he neglected governance for hunting and sport, indulged in revelry within the palace, and could not attend court until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong acceded, he neglected governance for hunting and sport, indulged in revelry within the palace, and could not attend court until dawn.

sentences.zh: 郾進曰：「十一聖之功德，四海之大，萬國之眾，其治其亂，系於陛下。

translations.literal: Yan advanced and said: "The merit of eleven sage emperors, the vastness of the Four Seas, the multitude of ten thousand states—whether there is order or disorder depends on Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yan advanced and said: "The merit of eleven sage emperors, the vastness of the Four Seas, the multitude of ten thousand states—whether there is order or disorder depends on Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 自山以東百城，地千里，昨日得之，今日失之。

translations.literal: From the mountains eastward lie a hundred prefectures across a thousand li of land—what was gained yesterday is lost today.
translations.idiomatic: From the mountains eastward lie a hundred prefectures across a thousand li of land—what was gained yesterday is lost today.

sentences.zh: 西望戎壘，距宗廟十舍，百姓憔悴，畜積無有。

translations.literal: Looking west to the frontier fortresses, only ten stages lie between them and the imperial ancestral temple; the common people are wasted, and stored provisions are gone.
translations.idiomatic: Looking west to the frontier fortresses, only ten stages lie between them and the imperial ancestral temple. The common people are wasted, and stored provisions are gone.

sentences.zh: 願陛下親政事以幸天下。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to attend personally to state affairs and bring good fortune to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to attend personally to state affairs and bring good fortune to the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝動容慰謝，遷給事中。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved in countenance and thanked him with words of comfort, then promoted him to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved in countenance and thanked him with words of comfort, then promoted him to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 敬宗嗣位，拜翰林侍講學士，旋進中書舍人，謝曰：「陛下使臣侍講，歷半歲不一問經義。

translations.literal: When Jingzong succeeded to the throne, Yan was appointed Hanlin Academician and Lecturer, and soon afterward was promoted to Palace Secretariat Drafting Official; he declined, saying: "Your Majesty appointed me to lecture, yet in half a year not once did you inquire about the meaning of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong succeeded to the throne, Yan was appointed Hanlin academician and lecturer, and soon afterward was promoted to palace secretariat drafting official. He declined, saying: "Your Majesty appointed me to lecture, yet in half a year not once did you inquire about the meaning of the classics.

sentences.zh: 臣無功，不足副厚恩。」

translations.literal: I have achieved nothing and am unworthy of such great favor.
translations.idiomatic: I have achieved nothing and am unworthy of such great favor.

sentences.zh: 帝慚曰：「朕少間當請益。」

translations.literal: The emperor said in shame: "When I have a little leisure I shall ask for instruction."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said in shame: "When I have a little leisure I shall ask for instruction."

sentences.zh: 高釴適在旁，因言：「陛下樂善而無所咨詢，天下之人不知有響儒意。」

translations.literal: Gao Li happened to be present and thereupon said: "Your Majesty delights in goodness yet consults no one; the people of the realm do not know that there is a Confucian scholar in attendance."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Li happened to be present and thereupon said: "Your Majesty delights in goodness yet consults no one. The people of the realm do not know that there is a Confucian scholar in attendance."

sentences.zh: 帝重咎謝，鹹賜錦、幣。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply reproached himself and apologized, and richly bestowed silk and cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply reproached himself and apologized, and richly bestowed silk and cash.

sentences.zh: 郾與高重類《六經》要言為十篇，上之，以便觀省。

translations.literal: Yan and Gao Chong compiled the essential teachings of the Six Classics into ten chapters and presented them to the throne for convenient reading.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Gao Chong compiled the essential teachings of the Six Classics into ten chapters and presented them to the throne for convenient reading.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎，出為虢州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and sent out as Observation Commissioner of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of rites and sent out as observation commissioner of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先是，上供財乏，則奪吏奉助輸，歲率八十萬。

translations.literal: Earlier, when funds for imperial tribute were short, officials' salaries were seized to help meet the quota, averaging eight hundred thousand per year.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when funds for imperial tribute were short, officials' salaries were seized to help meet the quota, averaging eight hundred thousand per year.

sentences.zh: 郾曰：「吏不能贍私，安暇恤民？

translations.literal: Yan said: "If officials cannot support themselves, how can they find time to care for the people?
translations.idiomatic: Yan said: "If officials cannot support themselves, how can they find time to care for the people?

sentences.zh: 吾不能獨治，安得自封？」

translations.literal: If I cannot govern alone, how can I enrich myself alone?
translations.idiomatic: If I cannot govern alone, how can I enrich myself alone?

sentences.zh: 即以府常費代之。

translations.literal: He thereupon used the prefecture's regular expenditures in place of the seized salaries.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon used the prefecture's regular expenditures in place of the seized salaries.

sentences.zh: 又詔賦粟輸太倉者，歲數萬石，民困於輸，則又輦而致之河。

translations.literal: There was also an edict requiring grain tribute to the imperial granary of tens of thousands of shi each year; the people were burdened by transport, and when that failed they were made to haul it to the river by cart.
translations.idiomatic: There was also an edict requiring grain tribute to the imperial granary of tens of thousands of shi each year. The people were burdened by transport, and when that failed they were made to haul it to the river by cart.

sentences.zh: 郾乃旁流為大敖受粟，竇而註諸艚。

translations.literal: Yan then diverted a side stream to build a large storage basin to receive the grain, opened channels, and channeled it into barges.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then diverted a side stream to build a large storage basin to receive the grain, opened channels, and channeled it into barges.

sentences.zh: 民悅，忘輸之勞。

translations.literal: The people were pleased and forgot the hardship of transport.
translations.idiomatic: The people were pleased and forgot the hardship of transport.

sentences.zh: 改鄂、嶽等州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Observation Commissioner of E, Yue, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to observation commissioner of E, Yue, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 自蔡人叛，鄂、嶽常苦兵，江湖盜賊顯行。

translations.literal: Since the people of Cai rebelled, E and Yue had constantly suffered from warfare, and bandits on the rivers and lakes operated openly.
translations.idiomatic: Since the people of Cai rebelled, E and Yue had constantly suffered from warfare, and bandits on the rivers and lakes operated openly.

sentences.zh: 郾修治鎧仗，造蒙沖，駛追窮躡，上下千里，歲中悉捕平。

translations.literal: Yan repaired armor and weapons, built covered assault boats, and with swift pursuit ran the bandits down; within a thousand li upstream and downstream, within the year all were captured and suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan repaired armor and weapons, built covered assault boats, and with swift pursuit ran the bandits down. Within a thousand li upstream and downstream, within the year all were captured and suppressed.

sentences.zh: 又觀察浙西，遷檢校禮部尚書，卒於官。

translations.literal: He also served as observation commissioner of Zhexi, was promoted to Acting Minister of Rites, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as observation commissioner of Zhexi, was promoted to acting minister of rites, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，謚曰德。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded the title Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous name De.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title minister of personnel, with the posthumous name De.

sentences.zh: 郾不藏貲，有輒周給親舊，為治其昏喪。

translations.literal: Yan did not hoard wealth; whenever he had any he would distribute it to relatives and old friends and arrange their weddings and funerals.
translations.idiomatic: Yan did not hoard wealth. Whenever he had any he would distribute it to relatives and old friends and arrange their weddings and funerals.

sentences.zh: 居家怡然，不訓子弟，子弟自化。

translations.literal: At home he was at ease and did not instruct his sons and nephews; they reformed themselves of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: At home he was at ease and did not instruct his sons and nephews. They reformed themselves of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 室處庳漏，無步廡，至霖淖，則客蓋而屐以就外位。

translations.literal: His dwelling was low and leaked, with no covered walk; when rain and mud came, guests would take umbrellas and clogs to reach the outer seats.
translations.idiomatic: His dwelling was low and leaked, with no covered walk. When rain and mud came, guests would take umbrellas and clogs to reach the outer seats.

sentences.zh: 治虢以寬，經月不笞一人。

translations.literal: In governing Guo he was lenient and for a month did not beat a single person.
translations.idiomatic: In governing Guo he was lenient and for a month did not beat a single person.

sentences.zh: 及涖鄂，則嚴法峻誅，一不貸。

translations.literal: When he arrived at E, he applied strict law and severe punishment and showed no mercy.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived at E, he applied strict law and severe punishment and showed no mercy.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，曰：「陜土瘠而民勞，吾撫之不暇，猶恐其擾；

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, he said: "The soil of Shaan is poor and the people labor hard; I have no leisure even to comfort them and still fear troubling them;
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked the reason, he said: "The soil of Shaan is poor and the people labor hard. I have no leisure even to comfort them and still fear troubling them;

sentences.zh: 鄂土沃民剽，雜以夷俗，非用威莫能治。

translations.literal: E's soil is fertile and the people are fierce, mixed with barbarian customs; without employing severity none can govern them.
translations.idiomatic: E's soil is fertile and the people are fierce, mixed with barbarian customs. Without employing severity, none can govern them.

sentences.zh: 政所以貴知變者也。」

translations.literal: This is why governance values knowing how to adapt."
translations.idiomatic: This is why governance values knowing how to adapt."

sentences.zh: 聞者服焉。

translations.literal: Those who heard were convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard were convinced.

sentences.zh: 五子：瑤、瑰、瑾、珮、璆。

translations.literal: Five sons: Yao, Gui, Jin, Pei, and Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Five sons: Yao, Gui, Jin, Pei, and Qiu.

sentences.zh: 瑤任禮部侍郎、浙西鄂嶽觀察使。

translations.literal: Yao served as vice minister of rites and Zhexi E-Yue observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yao served as vice minister of rites and Zhexi E-Yue observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 瑾禮部侍郎、湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Jin was vice minister of rites and Hunan observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was vice minister of rites and Hunan observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 瑰、珮俱達官。

translations.literal: Gui and Pei both reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and Pei both reached high office.

sentences.zh: 弟 鄯

translations.literal: Younger brother: Shan
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Shan

sentences.zh: 鄯，擢進士，累遷至左金吾衛大將軍，暴卒，以韓約代之。

translations.literal: Shan passed the jinshi examination and was promoted through successive posts to grand general of the Left Jinwu Guard; he died suddenly, and Han Yue was appointed to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Shan passed the jinshi examination and rose through successive posts to grand general of the Left Jinwu Guard. He died suddenly, and Han Yue was appointed to replace him.

sentences.zh: 不閱旬，李訓亂，約死於難。

translations.literal: Within ten days, Li Xun's rebellion broke out and Yue died in the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days, Li Xun's rebellion broke out and Yue died in the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 世謂鄯之亡，崔氏積善報也。

translations.literal: People of the time said Shan's death was karmic repayment for the Cui clan's accumulated virtue.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time said Shan's death was karmic repayment for the Cui clan's accumulated virtue.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 弟 鄲

translations.literal: Younger brother: Yin
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Yin

sentences.zh: 鄲及進士第，補渭南尉。

translations.literal: Yin passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: Yin passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 累除刑部郎中，出副杜元穎西川節度府。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Justice and sent out as deputy to Du Yuanying's Xichuan circuit headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Justice and sent out as deputy to Du Yuanying's Xichuan circuit headquarters.

sentences.zh: 召入為工部侍郎、集賢殿學士。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital as vice minister of works and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital as vice minister of works and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 再遷吏部侍郎，由宣歙觀察使入為太常卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to vice minister of personnel and, from Xuan-Xi observation commissioner, entered the capital as minister of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to vice minister of personnel and, from Xuan-Xi observation commissioner, entered the capital as minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 文宗末，擢同中書門下平章事，改中書侍郎，罷為劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Wenzong's reign he was promoted to associate director of the Secretariat and Chancellery, then changed to vice director of the Secretariat and dismissed to serve as military commissioner of Sword-South and Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Wenzong's reign he was promoted to associate director of the Secretariat and Chancellery, then changed to vice director of the Secretariat and dismissed to serve as military commissioner of Sword-South and Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，以檢校尚書右仆射同平章事，節度淮南，卒於軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanzong's reign he served as honorary right vice director of the Secretariat and associate director, military commissioner of Huainan, and died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanzong's reign he served as honorary right vice director of the Secretariat and associate director, military commissioner of Huainan, and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 崔氏四世緦麻同爨，兄弟六人至三品，邠、郾、鄲凡為禮部五，吏部再，唐興無有也。

translations.literal: For four generations the Cui clan wore the finest mourning garb and ate from a single kitchen; six brothers reached the third rank; Bin, Yan, and Yin together held the Ministry of Rites five times and the Ministry of Personnel twice — since the founding of Tang there had been nothing like it.
translations.idiomatic: For four generations the Cui clan wore the finest mourning garb and ate from a single kitchen. Six brothers reached the third rank; Bin, Yan, and Yin together held the Ministry of Rites five times and the Ministry of Personnel twice — since the founding of Tang there had been nothing like it.

sentences.zh: 居光德里，構便齋，宣宗聞而嘆曰：「鄲一門孝友，可為士族法。」

translations.literal: They lived in Guangde Lane and built a modest hall. When Emperor Xuanzong heard of it he sighed and said: "Yin's household is filial and friendly — it can serve as a model for gentry families."
translations.idiomatic: They lived in Guangde Lane and built a modest hall. When Emperor Xuanzong heard of it he sighed and said: "Yin's household is filial and friendly — it can serve as a model for gentry families."

sentences.zh: 因題曰「德星堂」。

translations.literal: He thereupon inscribed it "Hall of Virtuous Stars."
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon inscribed it "Hall of Virtuous Stars."

sentences.zh: 後京兆民即其裏為「德星社」云。

translations.literal: Later the people of the capital established at that lane a "Virtuous Stars Society."
translations.idiomatic: Later the people of the capital established at that lane a "Virtuous Stars Society."

sentences.zh: 柳公綽

translations.literal: Liu Gongchuo
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongchuo

sentences.zh: 柳公綽，字寬，京兆華原人。

translations.literal: Liu Gongchuo, courtesy name Kuan, was a native of Huayuan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongchuo, courtesy name Kuan, was a native of Huayuan in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 始生三日，伯父子華曰：「興吾門者，此兒也。」

translations.literal: Three days after his birth his uncle Zihua said: "He who will raise our house is this boy."
translations.idiomatic: Three days after his birth his uncle Zihua said: "He who will raise our house is this boy."

sentences.zh: 因小字起之。

translations.literal: He therefore gave him a childhood name based on this.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore gave him a childhood name based on this.

sentences.zh: 幼孝友，性質嚴重，起居皆有禮法。

translations.literal: As a child he was filial and friendly; his nature was stern and grave, and in rising and sitting he always observed ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was filial and friendly. His nature was stern and grave, and in rising and sitting he always observed ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 屬文典正，不讀非聖書。

translations.literal: His essays were classical and correct, and he did not read books that were not those of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: His essays were classical and correct, and he did not read books that were not those of the sages.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良方正直言極諫，補校書郎。

translations.literal: Recommended in the examination for filial and incorrupt, upright speech and extreme remonstrance, he was appointed proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended in the examination for filial and incorrupt, upright speech and extreme remonstrance, he was appointed proofreader.

sentences.zh: 間一年，再登其科，授渭南尉。

translations.literal: After one year he passed that examination again and was appointed assistant magistrate of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: After one year he passed that examination again and was appointed assistant magistrate of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 歲歉饉，其家雖給，而每飯不過一器，歲豐乃復。

translations.literal: In years of famine, though his household had provisions, at each meal he took no more than one dish; only in abundant years did he restore his former fare.
translations.idiomatic: In years of famine, though his household had provisions, at each meal he took no more than one dish. Only in abundant years did he restore his former fare.

sentences.zh: 或問之，答曰：「四方病饑，獨能飽乎？」

translations.literal: When someone asked him, he answered: "The four quarters suffer famine — can I alone eat my fill?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked him, he answered: "The four quarters suffer famine — can I alone eat my fill?"

sentences.zh: 累遷開州刺史，地接夷落，寇常逼其城，吏曰：「兵力不能制，願以右職署渠帥。」

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to prefect of Kai; the region bordered barbarian settlements, and bandits often pressed the city. The officials said: "Our military strength cannot control them; we wish to appoint the tribal chieftain to a high office."
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to prefect of Kai. The region bordered barbarian settlements, and bandits often pressed the city. The officials said: "Our military strength cannot control them; we wish to appoint the tribal chieftain to a high office."

sentences.zh: 公綽曰：「若同惡邪？

translations.literal: Gongchuo said: "Would that be sharing in evil?
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo said: "Would that be sharing in evil?

sentences.zh: 何可撓法！」

translations.literal: How could one bend the law!"
translations.idiomatic: How could one bend the law!"

sentences.zh: 立誅之，寇亦引去。

translations.literal: He immediately executed the man, and the bandits also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately executed the man, and the bandits also withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史、吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to attendant censor and assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant censor and assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時武元衡節度劍南，與裴度俱為判官，尤相引重。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanheng commanded Jiannan, he and Pei Du both served on his staff and held each other in especial esteem.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanheng commanded Jiannan, he and Pei Du both served on his staff and held each other in especial esteem.

sentences.zh: 召為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 憲宗喜武功，且數出遊畋，公綽奏《太醫箴》以諷曰：「天布寒暑，不私於人。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong delighted in military achievement and often went out hunting; Gongchuo submitted the "Admonition of the Grand Physician" to remonstrate, saying: "Heaven spreads cold and heat and shows favoritism to no one.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong delighted in military achievement and often went out hunting. Gongchuo submitted the "Admonition of the Grand Physician" to remonstrate, saying: "Heaven spreads cold and heat and shows favoritism to no one.

sentences.zh: 品類既一，高卑以均。

translations.literal: All living kinds are one; high and low are equal.
translations.idiomatic: All living kinds are one; high and low are equal.

sentences.zh: 人謹好愛，能保其身。

translations.literal: When people are careful in cherishing themselves, they can preserve their bodies.
translations.idiomatic: When people are careful in cherishing themselves, they can preserve their bodies.

sentences.zh: 清靜無瑕，輝光以新。

translations.literal: When pure and quiet without flaw, brilliance renews itself.
translations.idiomatic: When pure and quiet without flaw, brilliance renews itself.

sentences.zh: 寒暑滿天地，浹肌膚於外；

translations.literal: Cold and heat fill heaven and earth and soak the skin without;
translations.idiomatic: Cold and heat fill heaven and earth and soak the skin without;

sentences.zh: 好愛在耳目，誘心知於內。

translations.literal: What one loves fills ear and eye and seduces the mind within.
translations.idiomatic: What one loves fills ear and eye and seduces the mind within.

sentences.zh: 端潔為堤，奔射猶敗。

translations.literal: Upright purity serves as an embankment, yet rushing torrents still breach it.
translations.idiomatic: Upright purity serves as an embankment, yet rushing torrents still breach it.

sentences.zh: 氣行無間，隙不在大。

translations.literal: Qi flows without gap; the opening need not be large.
translations.idiomatic: Qi flows without gap; the opening need not be large.

sentences.zh: 謂天高矣，氛蒙晦之；

translations.literal: One says heaven is high, yet vapors cloud and darken it;
translations.idiomatic: One says heaven is high, yet vapors cloud and darken it;

sentences.zh: 謂地厚矣，橫流潰之。

translations.literal: One says earth is thick, yet cross-flowing waters breach it.
translations.idiomatic: One says earth is thick, yet cross-flowing waters breach it.

sentences.zh: 飲食資身，過則生患；

translations.literal: Food and drink sustain the body — excess then gives rise to illness;
translations.idiomatic: Food and drink sustain the body — excess then gives rise to illness;

sentences.zh: 衣服稱德，侈則生慢。

translations.literal: Clothes should match virtue — extravagance then gives rise to contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Clothes should match virtue — extravagance then gives rise to contempt.

sentences.zh: 唯過與侈，心必隨之。

translations.literal: Only excess and extravagance — the mind must follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Only excess and extravagance — the mind must follow them.

sentences.zh: 氣與心流，疾乃伺之。

translations.literal: Qi and mind flow together; disease then watches for its chance.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and mind flow together; disease then watches for its chance.

sentences.zh: 畋遊恣樂，流情蕩誌。

translations.literal: Hunting and roaming at will — feelings float and purpose slackens.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting and roaming at will — feelings float and purpose slackens.

sentences.zh: 馳騁勞形，叱咤傷氣。

translations.literal: Galloping wearies the form; shouting harms the breath.
translations.idiomatic: Galloping wearies the form; shouting harms the breath.

sentences.zh: 不養其外，前脩所忌。

translations.literal: Not nourishing the exterior — what former worthies forbade.
translations.idiomatic: Not nourishing the exterior — what former worthies forbade.

sentences.zh: 人乘氣生，嗜欲以萌。

translations.literal: People are born riding qi; appetites and desires thus sprout.
translations.idiomatic: People are born riding qi; appetites and desires thus sprout.

sentences.zh: 氣離有患，氣完則成。

translations.literal: When qi departs there is illness; when qi is complete then accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: When qi departs there is illness; when qi is complete then accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 巧必喪真，智實誘情。

translations.literal: Cleverness must lose genuineness; cunning in truth seduces the feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Cleverness must lose genuineness; cunning in truth seduces the feelings.

sentences.zh: 醫之上者，理於未然。

translations.literal: The superior physician treats principle before illness exists.
translations.idiomatic: The superior physician treats principle before illness exists.

sentences.zh: 患居慮後，防處事先。

translations.literal: Illness rests on concern afterward; defense lies in acting first.
translations.idiomatic: Illness rests on concern afterward; defense lies in acting first.

sentences.zh: 心靜樂行，體和道全。

translations.literal: Mind quiet, joy in conduct, body harmonious, the Way complete.
translations.idiomatic: Mind quiet, joy in conduct, body harmonious, the Way complete.

sentences.zh: 克施萬物，以享億年。

translations.literal: Able to bestow on the myriad things and enjoy myriad years.
translations.idiomatic: Able to bestow on the myriad things and enjoy myriad years.

sentences.zh: 聖人在上，各有攸處。

translations.literal: When the sage is above, each has his allotted place.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage is above, each has his allotted place.

sentences.zh: 臣司太醫，敢告諸禦。」

translations.literal: Your servant holds the post of grand physician and dares report to all who attend the emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds the post of grand physician and dares report to all who attend the emperor."

sentences.zh: 天子高其才，遣使謂曰：「卿言『氣行無間，隙不在大』，愛朕深者，當置之坐隅。」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven admired his talent and sent an envoy to say: "Your words, 'Qi flows without gap; the opening need not be large' — one who loves Us deeply should place this at Our sitting corner."
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven admired his talent and sent an envoy to say: "Your words, 'Qi flows without gap; the opening need not be large' — one who loves Us deeply should place this at Our sitting corner."

sentences.zh: 逾月，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: More than a month later he was appointed censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later he was appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 公綽本與裴垍善，李吉甫復當國，出為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Gongchuo had originally been on good terms with Pei Ji; when Li Jifu again held state power, he was sent out as Hunan observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo had originally been on good terms with Pei Ji. When Li Jifu again held state power, he was sent out as Hunan observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以地卑濕，不可迎養，求分司東都，不聽。

translations.literal: Because the region was low and damp and unsuitable for receiving and caring for his parents, he requested a post in the Eastern Capital branch office, but permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Because the region was low and damp and unsuitable for receiving and caring for his parents, he requested a post in the Eastern Capital branch office, but permission was not granted.

sentences.zh: 後徙鄂嶽觀察使。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to E-Yue observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to E-Yue observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時方討吳元濟，詔發鄂嶽卒五千，隸安州刺史李聽。

translations.literal: At that time the court was campaigning against Wu Yuanji; an edict dispatched five thousand E-Yue troops placed under An Prefecture governor Li Ting.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was campaigning against Wu Yuanji. An edict dispatched five thousand E-Yue troops placed under An Prefecture governor Li Ting.

sentences.zh: 公綽曰：「朝廷謂吾儒生不知兵邪！」

translations.literal: Gongchuo said: "Does the court think this Confucian scholar knows nothing of war?"
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo said: "Does the court think this Confucian scholar knows nothing of war?"

sentences.zh: 即請自行，許之。

translations.literal: He immediately requested to lead them himself, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately requested to lead them himself, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 引兵度江，抵安州，聽以軍禮迎謁。

translations.literal: He led the troops across the river and arrived at An Prefecture; Ting received him with military ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He led the troops across the river and arrived at An Prefecture. Ting received him with military ceremony.

sentences.zh: 公綽謂曰：「公所以屬負弩，豈非兵事邪？

translations.literal: Gongchuo said to him: "The reason you were assigned the crossbow-bearers — was it not a military matter?
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo said to him: "The reason you were assigned the crossbow-bearers — was it not a military matter?

sentences.zh: 若褫戎容，則兩郡守耳，何所統壹哉？

translations.literal: If you strip off military garb, we are merely two prefectural governors — what unified command is there?
translations.idiomatic: If you strip off military garb, we are merely two prefectural governors — what unified command is there?

sentences.zh: 以公世將曉兵，吾且欲署職，以兵法從事。」

translations.literal: Since your family for generations has been military and understands warfare, I intend to grant you a post and have you conduct affairs according to military law."
translations.idiomatic: Since your family for generations has been military and understands warfare, I intend to grant you a post and have you conduct affairs according to military law."

sentences.zh: 聽曰：「唯命。」

translations.literal: Ting said: "As you command."
translations.idiomatic: Ting said: "As you command."

sentences.zh: 即以都知兵馬使、中軍先鋒、行營都虞候三牒授之，選兵六千屬焉，戒諸校曰：「行營事一決都將。」

translations.literal: He thereupon granted him three commissions — director knowing military affairs, vanguard of the central army, and chief camp adjutant — selected six thousand troops under his command, and warned the officers: "Camp affairs shall be decided solely by the commanding general."
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon granted him three commissions — director knowing military affairs, vanguard of the central army, and chief camp adjutant — selected six thousand troops under his command, and warned the officers: "Camp affairs shall be decided solely by the commanding general."

sentences.zh: 聽被用畏威，遂盡力，當時服其知權。

translations.literal: Once employed, Ting feared his authority and exerted himself fully; at the time people admired his knowing how to wield authority.
translations.idiomatic: Once employed, Ting feared his authority and exerted himself fully. At the time people admired his knowing how to wield authority.

sentences.zh: 軍出，公綽數省問其家，疾病生死厚給之，婦人敖蕩者，沈之江。

translations.literal: When the army went out, Gongchuo repeatedly visited their families, generously providing for illness, birth, and death; women who were licentious were drowned in the river.
translations.idiomatic: When the army went out, Gongchuo repeatedly visited their families, generously providing for illness, birth, and death. Women who were licentious were drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 軍中感服曰：「中丞為我知家事，敢不死戰！」

translations.literal: The army was deeply moved and said: "The commissioner takes care of our household affairs for us — how dare we not fight to the death!"
translations.idiomatic: The army was deeply moved and said: "The commissioner takes care of our household affairs for us — how dare we not fight to the death!"

sentences.zh: 故鄂軍每戰輒克。

translations.literal: Therefore the E troops whenever they fought always prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the E troops whenever they fought always prevailed.

sentences.zh: 元和十一年，為李道古代還，除給事中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yuanhe he replaced Li Daogu and was appointed supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yuanhe he replaced Li Daogu and was appointed supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 李師道平，遣宣諭鄆州，復命，拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: When Li Shidao was pacified he was dispatched to proclaim the news at Yan Prefecture; upon returning from his mission he was appointed governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shidao was pacified he was dispatched to proclaim the news at Yan Prefecture. Upon returning from his mission he was appointed governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 方赴府，有神策校乘馬不避者，即時搒死。

translations.literal: Just as he was proceeding to the yamen, a Shence Army officer rode a horse and did not yield — Gongchuo immediately had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was proceeding to the yamen, a Shence Army officer rode a horse and did not yield. Gongchuo immediately had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 帝怒其專殺，公綽曰：「此非獨試臣，乃輕陛下法。」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry at his unauthorized killing; Gongchuo said: "This was not merely testing your servant — it was slighting Your Majesty's law."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry at his unauthorized killing. Gongchuo said: "This was not merely testing your servant — it was slighting Your Majesty's law."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「既死，不以聞，可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Since he is dead, not reporting it — is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Since he is dead, not reporting it — is that acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 公綽曰：「臣不當奏。

translations.literal: Gongchuo said: "Your servant ought not to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo said: "Your servant ought not to memorialize.

sentences.zh: 在市死，職金吾；

translations.literal: If he dies in the market, that is the duty of the Jinwu;
translations.idiomatic: If he dies in the market, that is the duty of the Jinwu;

sentences.zh: 在坊死，職左右巡使。」

translations.literal: if he dies in the ward, that is the duty of the left and right patrol commissioners."
translations.idiomatic: if he dies in the ward, that is the duty of the left and right patrol commissioners."

sentences.zh: 帝乃解。

translations.literal: The emperor then understood.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then understood.

sentences.zh: 以母喪去官。

translations.literal: He left office due to his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office due to his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，為刑部侍郎，領鹽鐵轉運使，轉兵部，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended he served as vice minister of justice and headed the salt and iron transport commission, then transferred to the Ministry of War while concurrently serving as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended he served as vice minister of justice and headed the salt and iron transport commission, then transferred to the Ministry of War while concurrently serving as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，復為京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing he again became governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing he again became governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 時幽、鎮用兵，補置諸將，使驲系道。

translations.literal: At that time You and Zhen were at war; supplemental appointments of various generals sent courier horses tying up the roads.
translations.idiomatic: At that time You and Zhen were at war. Supplemental appointments of various generals sent courier horses tying up the roads.

sentences.zh: 公綽奏曰：「比館遞匱乏，驛置多闕。

translations.literal: Gongchuo memorialized: "Recently relay stations are depleted and deficient, and post stations are mostly lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo memorialized: "Recently relay stations are depleted and deficient, and post stations are mostly lacking.

sentences.zh: 敕使衣緋紫者，所乘至三四十騎；

translations.literal: Imperial envoys wearing crimson and purple ride with as many as thirty or forty horses;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial envoys wearing crimson and purple ride with as many as thirty or forty horses;

sentences.zh: 黃綠者，不下十數。

translations.literal: those in yellow and green, no fewer than ten or so.
translations.idiomatic: those in yellow and green, no fewer than ten or so.

sentences.zh: 吏不得視券，隨口輒供。

translations.literal: Officials could not examine the vouchers; on whatever was spoken they at once supplied [horses].
translations.idiomatic: Officials were not allowed to check the vouchers and supplied horses on whatever was demanded at once.

sentences.zh: 驛馬盡，乃掠奪民馬。

translations.literal: When post horses were exhausted, they then plundered civilian horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the relay horses ran out, they seized the people's horses instead.

sentences.zh: 怨嗟驚擾，行李殆絕。

translations.literal: Complaints, alarm, and disturbance; travelers' baggage nearly ceased entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Grumbling and panic spread, and ordinary travelers all but disappeared from the roads.

sentences.zh: 請著定限，以息其弊。」

translations.literal: I request fixed limits be established to end this abuse."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that fixed quotas be set to put an end to these abuses."

sentences.zh: 有詔中書條檢定數，由是吏得紓罪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Secretariat to compile and verify fixed numbers, and thereby officials could be relieved of blame.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Secretariat to draw up and verify fixed quotas, and from then on the clerks could escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 宦官共惡疾之。

translations.literal: The eunuchs all hated him bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs all loathed him intensely.

sentences.zh: 改吏部侍郎，遷御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of personnel and promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 韓弘病，自河中還，詔百官問疾，弘遣子辭不能見，公綽謂曰：「上使百司省候，是謂異禮，宜力疾以見公卿，安可臥令子姓傳言耶？」

translations.literal: Han Hong fell ill and returned from Hezhong. The emperor ordered all officials to inquire after his health. Hong sent his son to decline, saying he could not receive visitors. Gongchuo said to him: "The emperor has sent all the bureaus to pay their respects — this is an extraordinary honor. You should force yourself to appear despite your illness to meet the nobles and ministers. How can you lie abed and have your son relay your words?"
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong fell ill and returned from Hezhong. The emperor ordered the whole bureaucracy to inquire after his health, but Hong sent his son to say he was too ill to receive visitors. Gongchuo told him, "The emperor has sent every office to call on you — that is an extraordinary courtesy. You ought to rouse yourself despite your illness and receive the chief ministers in person. How can you stay in bed and send your son to speak for you?"

sentences.zh: 弘懼，挾扶以出。

translations.literal: Hong was afraid and was assisted out leaning on support.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was frightened and had himself helped outside.

sentences.zh: 改禮部尚書，以祖諱換左丞。

translations.literal: He was changed to minister of rites; because of his grandfather's taboo name, he exchanged the post for left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of rites, but because of his grandfather's taboo name he was reassigned as left vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校戶部尚書、山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed acting minister of revenue and military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was named acting minister of revenue and military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 行部至鄧，縣吏有納賄、舞文二人同系獄，縣令以公綽素持法，謂必殺貪者，公綽判曰：「贓吏犯法，法在；

translations.literal: On a tour of his circuit he reached Deng. Two county clerks — one who took bribes and one who manipulated documents — were imprisoned together. The county magistrate, knowing Gongchuo always upheld the law, assumed he would certainly execute the corrupt one. Gongchuo judged: "The corrupt official violates the law — the law remains.
translations.idiomatic: While touring his circuit he reached Deng, where two county clerks — one who took bribes and one who twisted the law in writing — were imprisoned together. The magistrate, knowing Gongchuo's reputation for strict justice, assumed he would surely execute the bribe-taker. Gongchuo ruled, "When a corrupt official breaks the law, the law still stands.

sentences.zh: 奸吏壞法，法亡。」

translations.literal: When a scheming official destroys the law, the law perishes."
translations.idiomatic: When a scheming official destroys the law, the law itself is lost.

sentences.zh: 誅舞文者。

translations.literal: He executed the document-manipulating one.
translations.idiomatic: He executed the clerk who had twisted the law.

sentences.zh: 其廄馬害圉人，公綽殺之。

translations.literal: A stable horse in his stables harmed a groom; Gongchuo had it killed.
translations.idiomatic: One of his stable horses injured a groom, and Gongchuo had the horse killed.

sentences.zh: 或言良馬可愛，曰：「安有良馬而害人乎？」

translations.literal: Some said it was a fine horse and lovable. He said: "How can there be a fine horse that harms people?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone said it was a fine horse and a pity to lose, he replied, "What fine horse ever harmed people?"

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年，就遷檢校左仆射。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoli he was promoted in place to acting vice director of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoli he was promoted on the spot to acting vice director of the Left.

sentences.zh: 牛僧孺罷政事，為武昌節度使，公綽具軍容伏謁，左右諫止之，答曰：「奇章始去臺宰，方鎮重宰相，所以尊朝廷也。」

translations.literal: Niu Sengru left the government and became military commissioner of Wuchang. Gongchuo put on full military dress and prostrated himself to pay respects. His attendants advised him to stop, but he replied: "Qizhang has just left the chancellorship; the regional commanders honor a former chancellor to show respect for the court."
translations.idiomatic: When Niu Sengru left the central government to become military commissioner of Wuchang, Gongchuo appeared in full military regalia and prostrated himself in greeting. His attendants tried to stop him, but he answered, "Qizhang has just stepped down from the chancellorship. A frontier commander who honors a former chancellor is honoring the court itself.

sentences.zh: 有道士獻丹藥，問所從來，曰：「自薊門。」

translations.literal: A Daoist priest presented elixir medicine. When asked where it came from, he said: "From Jimen."
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist priest offered him an elixir. Asked where it came from, the priest said, "From Jimen Gate.

sentences.zh: 時朱克融方叛，遽曰：「惜哉，藥自賊境來，雖驗何益！」

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Kerong had just rebelled. Gongchuo immediately said: "What a pity! The medicine comes from rebel territory — even if it works, what good is it!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kerong had just rebelled, and Gongchuo said at once, "What a pity — the medicine comes from rebel territory. Even if it works, what use is it?

sentences.zh: 即棄藥而逐道士。

translations.literal: He immediately discarded the medicine and expelled the Daoist.
translations.idiomatic: He threw the medicine away and drove the priest out.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部尚書，俄拜邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as minister of justice and soon was appointed military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as minister of justice and was soon appointed military commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 先是神策諸鎮列屯部中，不聽本道節制，故虜得窺間。

translations.literal: Previously the various Shence garrison units were stationed in columns in the prefecture and did not obey the local circuit commander's control, so the barbarians could exploit gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Shence garrisons had been posted in force throughout the prefecture and refused to take orders from the local commander, which let the barbarians probe for openings.

sentences.zh: 公綽論所宜，因詔屯營緩急悉受節度。

translations.literal: Gongchuo discussed what should be done, and consequently an edict ordered that garrison camps in emergencies all accept his command.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo laid out what ought to be done, and an edict followed requiring all garrison camps to obey his orders in emergencies.

sentences.zh: 復為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He again served as minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He again became minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 京兆獄有姑鞭婦至死者，府欲殺之。

translations.literal: In a Jingzhao prison case, a mother-in-law whipped her daughter-in-law to death, and the prefecture wanted to execute her.
translations.idiomatic: A Jingzhao case involved a mother-in-law who beat her daughter-in-law to death with a whip, and the prefectural office wanted to put her to death.

sentences.zh: 公綽曰：「尊毆卑，非鬥也；

translations.literal: Gongchuo said: "When a superior beats an inferior, it is not mutual combat.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo said, "When an elder strikes a junior, that is not a fight between equals.

sentences.zh: 且子在，以妻而戮其母，不順。」

translations.literal: Moreover, her son is alive — to execute the mother because of the wife would be unfilial."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, her son is still alive — to execute a mother because of a wife would violate filial duty.

sentences.zh: 遂減論。

translations.literal: The sentence was accordingly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The penalty was reduced accordingly.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，為河東節度。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he became military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe he became military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 遭歲惡，撙節用度，輟宴飲，衣食與士卒鈞。

translations.literal: Encountering a bad harvest year, he economized expenditures, stopped banquets and drinking, and shared food and clothing equally with the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When the harvest failed, he tightened spending, gave up feasting and drinking, and ate and dressed no better than his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 北虜遣梅祿將軍李暢以馬萬匹來市，所過皆厚勞，飭兵以防襲奪。

translations.literal: The northern barbarians sent General Meiluo's officer Li Chang with ten thousand horses to trade. Everywhere they passed they were lavishly entertained, and troops were deployed to guard against raids and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: The northern tribes sent Li Chang, an officer of General Meiluo, with ten thousand horses to trade. Every district along the route entertained them lavishly and kept troops ready to prevent raids and seizure.

sentences.zh: 至太原，公綽獨使牙將單騎勞問，待以至意，辟牙門，令譯官引謁，宴不加常。

translations.literal: When they reached Taiyuan, Gongchuo alone sent a guard officer on a single horse to welcome and inquire after them. He received them with utmost courtesy, opened the gate of his headquarters, had the interpreter conduct the audience, and held no extraordinary banquet.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan, Gongchuo sent only one guard officer on a single horse to welcome them. He received them with the utmost courtesy, opened his headquarters gate, had an interpreter conduct the audience, and offered no special banquet.

sentences.zh: 暢德之，出涕，徐驅道中，不妄馳獵。

translations.literal: Li Chang was grateful, shed tears, and slowly drove along the road without recklessly galloping or hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chang was moved by the courtesy, wept openly, and moved slowly along the road without reckless galloping or hunting.

sentences.zh: 陘北有沙陀部，勇武喜鬥，為九姓、六州所畏。

translations.literal: North of the Xing Gorge was the Shatuo tribe — brave and martial, fond of fighting — feared by the Nine Surnames and Six Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Xing Gorge lived the Shatuo, a people fierce in battle and eager to fight, feared by the Nine Surnames and Six Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 公綽召其酋朱邪執宜，治廢柵十一，募兵三千留屯塞上，其妻、母來太原者，令夫人飲食問遺之。

translations.literal: Gongchuo summoned their chieftain Zhuxie Zhuyi, repaired eleven abandoned stockades, recruited three thousand troops to garrison the frontier, and when their wives and mothers came to Taiyuan, had his lady provide food, drink, and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo summoned their chieftain Zhuxie Zhuyi, restored eleven abandoned stockades, and recruited three thousand men to garrison the border. When Shatuo wives and mothers came to Taiyuan, he had his own wife feed them and send gifts.

sentences.zh: 沙陀感恩，故悉力保鄣。

translations.literal: The Shatuo were grateful and therefore exerted all their strength to guard the border fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful, the Shatuo threw all their strength into defending the frontier.

sentences.zh: 以病乞代，授兵部尚書，不任朝請。

translations.literal: Ill, he requested a replacement and was appointed minister of war, exempt from court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to ask for relief; he was made minister of war but excused from attending court.

sentences.zh: 忽顧左右召故吏韋長，眾謂屬諉以家事。

translations.literal: Suddenly he looked around and summoned his former clerk Wei Zhang. Everyone thought he was entrusting household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he turned and summoned his former clerk Wei Zhang. Everyone assumed he meant to entrust him with family business.

sentences.zh: 及長至，乃曰：「為我白宰相，徐州專殺李聽親吏，非用高瑀不能安。」

translations.literal: When Zhang arrived, he said: "Tell the chancellor for me: Xuzhou arbitrarily executed Li Ting's personal clerk — only by appointing Gao Yu can there be peace."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang came, he said, "Tell the chancellor for me: Xuzhou has executed Li Ting's personal clerk on its own authority. Only by appointing Gao Yu can the region be pacified.

sentences.zh: 因瞑目不復語，後二日卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: He then closed his eyes and spoke no more. Two days later he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He closed his eyes and said no more. Two days later he died, at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚曰元。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince; posthumous title Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince, with the posthumous name Yuan.

sentences.zh: 公綽居喪毀慕，三年不澡沐。

translations.literal: Gongchuo during mourning was consumed by grief; for three years he did not bathe or wash.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning Gongchuo was so stricken with grief that for three years he would not bathe or wash.

sentences.zh: 事後母薛謹甚，雖姻屬不知非薛所生。

translations.literal: He served his stepmother Lady Xue with utmost respect; even in-laws did not know she was not his birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: He served his stepmother Lady Xue with scrupulous devotion, and even relatives by marriage did not know she was not his own mother.

sentences.zh: 外兄薛宮早卒，為育其女嫁之。

translations.literal: His maternal cousin Xue Gong died young; he raised his daughter and married her off.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal cousin Xue Gong died young, and Gongchuo raised his daughter and saw her married.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾蒞官未嘗以私喜怒加於人，子孫其昌乎！」

translations.literal: He once said: "In my official career I have never imposed private likes or dislikes on anyone — surely my descendants will prosper!"
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "In office I have never let private likes or dislikes govern how I treat people. Surely my descendants will flourish!

sentences.zh: 與錢徽、蔣乂、杜元穎、薛存誠善，取士如許康佐、鄭朗、盧簡辭、崔玙、夏侯孜、李拭、韋長，皆知名顯貴云。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Qian Hui, Jiang Yi, Du Yuanying, and Xue Cuncheng. Those he recommended for office, such as Xu Kangzuo, Zheng Lang, Lu Jianchi, Cui Yu, Xiahou Zi, Li Shi, and Wei Zhang, all became famous and prominent officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Qian Hui, Jiang Yi, Du Yuanying, and Xue Cuncheng. Men he recommended — Xu Kangzuo, Zheng Lang, Lu Jianchi, Cui Yu, Xiahou Zi, Li Shi, and Wei Zhang among them — all rose to fame and high rank.

sentences.zh: 子仲郢，字諭蒙。

translations.literal: His son Zhongying, courtesy name Yimeng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhongying, courtesy name Yimeng.

sentences.zh: 母韓，即臯女也，善訓子，故仲郢幼嗜學，嘗和熊膽丸，使夜咀咽以助勤。

translations.literal: His mother was Lady Han, daughter of Gao, skilled at instructing her son; therefore Zhongying from childhood loved learning. She once mixed bear-gall pills for him to chew and swallow at night to aid his diligence.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Han, a daughter of Gao, and she was skilled at teaching her son. From childhood Zhongying loved study; she once prepared pills of bear gall for him to chew at night to keep him at his books.

sentences.zh: 長工文，著《尚書二十四司箴》，為韓愈咨賞。

translations.literal: When grown he excelled at literary composition, wrote "Admonitions for the Twenty-Four Bureaus of the Ministry of Works," and won Han Yu's praise.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he excelled at writing and composed Admonitions for the Twenty-Four Bureaus of the Ministry of Works, which Han Yu praised highly.

sentences.zh: 元和末，及進士第，為校書郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination and became a collator.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a collator.

sentences.zh: 牛僧孺辟武昌幕府，有父風矩，僧孺嘆曰：「非積習名教，安及此邪？」

translations.literal: Niu Sengru recruited him to his Wuchang staff. He had his father's bearing and standards. Niu Sengru sighed: "Without long cultivation in the teachings of civilization, how could one reach this?"
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru recruited him to his staff at Wuchang. He carried himself with his father's dignity and discipline, and Niu Sengru sighed, "Without long training in the rites and teachings, how could anyone reach this?

sentences.zh: 入為監察御史，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as a supervisory censor and was promoted to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as a supervisory censor and was promoted to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 有禁卒誣裏人斫父墓柏，射殺之，吏以專殺論，而中尉護免其死，右補闕蔣系爭，不省。

translations.literal: An imperial guard soldier falsely accused a neighbor of cutting the cypress at his father's tomb and shot him dead. The officials proposed capital punishment for unauthorized killing, but the palace commandant shielded him and exempted him from death. Right remonstrance-supplementor Jiang Xi protested, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial guard falsely accused a neighbor of cutting the cypress at his father's tomb and shot the man dead. The officials sought a sentence for unauthorized killing, but the palace commandant protected him and spared his life. Right remonstrance-supplementor Jiang Xi protested, but no one listened.

sentences.zh: 仲郢監罰，執曰：「賊不死，是亂典刑。」

translations.literal: Zhongying oversaw the punishment and insisted: "If this criminal does not die, it is a corruption of standard punishments."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongying supervised the punishment and insisted, "If this killer is not put to death, the law itself is corrupted.

sentences.zh: 有詔御史蕭傑監之，傑復爭。

translations.literal: An edict ordered censor Xiao Jie to oversee it; Jie again protested.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered censor Xiao Jie to supervise the case, and Jie protested again.

sentences.zh: 遂獨詔京兆杖之，不監。

translations.literal: Finally an edict alone ordered the Jingzhao office to beat him, without oversight.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the emperor ordered Jingzhao alone to beat the man, with no censor present.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其守。

translations.literal: The court praised his steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，累轉吏部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang he was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Huichang era he rose through several posts to director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時詔減官冗長者，仲郢條簡浹日，損千二百五十員，議者厭伏。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered reduction of redundant officials. Zhongying compiled and simplified them in ten days, cutting 1,250 positions. Commentators were awed into silence.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict came to cut redundant posts, Zhongying sorted and trimmed the roster in ten days, eliminating 1,250 positions and silencing every critic.

sentences.zh: 遷左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left remonstrance adviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left remonstrance adviser.

sentences.zh: 武宗延方士，築望仙臺，累諫諄切，帝遣中人愧諭。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong entertained Daoist alchemists and built the Terrace of Gazing on Immortals. Zhongying repeatedly remonstrated earnestly and forcefully; the emperor sent a palace emissary to admonish and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong entertained Daoist adepts and built the Terrace of Gazing on Immortals. Zhongying remonstrated again and again, bluntly and at length, until the emperor sent a palace envoy to rebuke and warn him.

sentences.zh: 御史崔元藻以覆按吳湘獄得罪，仲郢切諫，宰相李德裕不為嫌，奏拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: Censor Cui Yuanzao was punished for reviewing the Wu Xiang case. Zhongying remonstrated forcefully. Chancellor Li Deyu held no grudge and memorialized to appoint him governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When censor Cui Yuanzao was punished for reinvestigating the Wu Xiang case, Zhongying remonstrated sharply. Chancellor Li Deyu bore no resentment and recommended him as governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 置權量於東西市，使貿易用之，禁私制者。

translations.literal: He placed standard weights and measures in the East and West Markets for traders to use and forbade private manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: He placed official weights and measures in the East and West Markets for merchants to use and banned private manufacture.

sentences.zh: 北司吏入粟違約，仲郢殺而屍之，自是人無敢犯，政號嚴明。

translations.literal: A Northern Bureau clerk violated terms on grain tribute. Zhongying executed him and displayed the corpse. From then on no one dared offend; his governance was called strict and clear.
translations.idiomatic: When a Northern Bureau clerk violated the terms on grain deliveries, Zhongying executed him and put the body on display. After that no one dared cross him, and his rule was known for its severity and clarity.

sentences.zh: 會廢浮屠法，盡壞銅象為錢。

translations.literal: When Buddhism was abolished, all copper Buddha images were melted for coin.
translations.idiomatic: When the suppression of Buddhism came, every copper Buddha image was destroyed and cast into coin.

sentences.zh: 仲郢為鑄錢使，吏請以字識錢者，不答。

translations.literal: Zhongying served as coinage commissioner. When clerks asked to mark coins with characters, he did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongying served as coinage commissioner. When clerks asked to stamp the coins with identifying characters, he gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 既，淮南鑄會昌字，久之，僧反取為鐘鈸云。

translations.literal: Later Huainan cast coins with the character "Huichang." After a long time, monks reclaimed them for bells and gongs.
translations.idiomatic: Later Huainan cast coins marked with the reign name Huichang, and in time the monks reclaimed the metal for bells and gongs.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人紇幹訴甥劉詡毆其母，詡為禁軍校，仲郢不待奏，即捕取之，死杖下，宦官以為言，改右散騎常侍，知吏部銓。

translations.literal: Secretariat drafter Heggan complained that his nephew Liu Xu beat his mother. Xu was a guard army officer. Zhongying, without waiting for a memorial, immediately arrested him. He died under the rod. Eunuchs complained; Zhongying was changed to right regular attendant and placed in charge of personnel selection.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter Heggan complained that his nephew Liu Xu had beaten his mother. Xu was an officer in the imperial guard. Without waiting for an imperial order, Zhongying had him arrested and beaten to death. When eunuchs protested, he was moved to right regular attendant and put in charge of personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 德裕頗抑進士科，仲郢無所徇。

translations.literal: Li Deyu had greatly suppressed the jinshi examination; Zhongying yielded to no one.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu had worked hard to curb the jinshi examination, but Zhongying bowed to no pressure.

sentences.zh: 是時，以進士選，無受惡官者。

translations.literal: At this time, in jinshi selection, no corrupt officials were admitted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, in selecting jinshi degree holders, no tainted official was accepted.

sentences.zh: 又當調者，持闕簿令自閱，即擬唱，吏無能為奸。

translations.literal: Also, when it came time for appointments, he had candidates hold the vacancy register and review it themselves; he then immediately proposed and announced appointments, and clerks could not commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: When appointments came due, he let each candidate read the vacancy register for himself, then immediately proposed and announced the posting, leaving the clerks no room for trickery.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，德裕罷政事，坐所厚善，出為鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanzong's reign, Li Deyu left the government. Because of their close friendship, Zhongying was sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuanzong's reign, when Li Deyu fell from power, Zhongying was sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou on account of their close friendship.

sentences.zh: 周墀鎮滑，而鄭為屬郡，高其績；

translations.literal: Zhou Chi governed Hua, and Zheng was a subordinate prefecture. Zhou held his performance in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chi governed Hua, with Zheng as a subordinate prefecture, and thought highly of Zhongying's record there.

sentences.zh: 及入相，薦授河南尹，召拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhou entered the chancellorship, he recommended Zhongying for governor of Henan and summoned him as vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou became chancellor, he recommended Zhongying for governor of Henan and had him recalled as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 墀罷，它宰相惡仲郢，左遷秘書監。

translations.literal: When Zhou left office, other chancellors disliked Zhongying and demoted him to director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou left office, other chancellors turned against Zhongying and demoted him to director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 數月，復出河南尹，以寬惠為政。

translations.literal: After several months he again went out as governor of Henan, governing with leniency and benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he was again sent out as governor of Henan, where he governed with leniency and kindness.

sentences.zh: 或言不類京兆時，答曰：「輦轂之下，先彈壓；

translations.literal: When some said this was unlike his time in Jingzhao, he replied: "Under the imperial chariot wheels, one first suppresses and restrains.
translations.idiomatic: When people said this was nothing like his days in Jingzhao, he answered, "Under the imperial capital one must first suppress wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 郡邑之治，本惠養。

translations.literal: Governance of commandery and county towns is fundamentally about nurturing with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Governing a commandery or county is fundamentally about caring for the people.

sentences.zh: 烏可類乎？」

translations.literal: How can the two be alike?"
translations.idiomatic: How can the two be the same?

sentences.zh: 擢劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military commissioner of Jiannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to military commissioner of Jiannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大吏邊章簡挾勢肆貪，前帥不能制，仲郢因事殺之，官下肅然。

translations.literal: A senior clerk, Bian Zhangjian, relied on his power and indulged in corruption; the previous commander could not control him. Zhongying seized an opportunity to execute him, and the officialdom became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: A senior clerk named Bian Zhangjian abused his power and plundered freely; the previous commander could not restrain him. Zhongying seized an occasion to execute him, and the whole administration fell into order.

sentences.zh: 居五年，召為吏部侍郎，俄改兵部，領鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: After five years he was recalled as vice minister of personnel; soon changed to vice minister of war and headed the salt and iron transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: After five years he was recalled as vice minister of personnel, then soon made vice minister of war and put in charge of the salt and iron transport commission.

sentences.zh: 有劉習者，以藥術進，詔署鹽官。

translations.literal: One Liu Xi, who advanced through medical arts, was ordered appointed salt official.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Liu Xi, who had risen through medical skill, was ordered appointed to a salt post.

sentences.zh: 仲郢以為醫有本色官，若委錢谷，名分不正。

translations.literal: Zhongying held that physicians had their proper official posts; to assign them finance and grain affairs would be an improper title and role.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongying argued that physicians already had posts suited to their profession, and to put them in charge of money and grain would violate proper rank and duty.

sentences.zh: 帝悟，乃賜縑遣還。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and gave him silk to send him home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the point, gave Liu Xi a gift of silk, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 大中十二年，辭疾，以刑部尚書罷使，轉戶部，封河東縣男，為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dazhong he declined due to illness, resigned the commission as minister of justice, transferred to minister of revenue, was enfeoffed as Baron of Hedong County, and became military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Dazhong he asked leave for illness, gave up his commission as minister of justice, moved to minister of revenue, was enfeoffed as Baron of Hedong County, and became military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 南鄭令權弈以罪，仲郢杖之，六日死，貶雷州刺史。

translations.literal: Nanzheng magistrate Quan Yi was guilty of an offense; Zhongying beat him with rods. He died on the sixth day. Zhongying was demoted to prefect of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanzheng magistrate Quan Yi was found guilty of an offense, Zhongying had him beaten with rods; he died on the sixth day, and Zhongying was demoted to prefect of Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以太子賓客分司東都，起為虢州刺史，以檢校尚書左仆射東都留守。

translations.literal: Soon he served as guest of the crown prince with duty at the Eastern Capital. He was raised to prefect of Guo and appointed acting vice director of the Left as Eastern Capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he served as guest of the crown prince with duty at the Eastern Capital, then was recalled as prefect of Guo and appointed acting vice director of the Left as Eastern Capital garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 會盜發父墓，棄官歸華原。

translations.literal: When robbers opened his father's tomb, he resigned office and returned to Huayuan.
translations.idiomatic: When robbers broke into his father's tomb, he resigned his post and returned to Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 徙華州刺史，不拜。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Hua but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Hua but refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 咸通五年，為天平節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xiantong he became military commissioner of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xiantong he became military commissioner of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 初，仲郢為諫議大夫，後每遷，必烏集升平第，庭樹戟架皆滿，五日乃散。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhongying was remonstrance adviser, whenever he was later promoted, crows would gather at his Shengping residence, filling the courtyard trees and ji racks, dispersing only after five days.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongying had been remonstrance adviser, every later promotion brought crows flocking to his Shengping residence until the courtyard trees and halberd racks were black with them; they would not disperse for five days.

sentences.zh: 及是不復集。

translations.literal: This time they no longer gathered.
translations.idiomatic: This time they did not gather.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮。

translations.literal: He died in his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his command.

sentences.zh: 仲郢方嚴，尚氣義，事親甚謹。

translations.literal: Zhongying was upright and stern, valued honor and righteousness, and was very dutiful toward his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongying was upright and severe, devoted to honor and principle, and extremely careful in serving his parents.

sentences.zh: 李德裕貶死，家無祿，不自振；

translations.literal: Li Deyu died in exile; his family had no stipend and could not support itself.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Deyu died in exile his household had no stipend and could not support itself.

sentences.zh: 及領鹽鐵，遂取其兄子從質為推官，知蘇州院。

translations.literal: When Zhongying took charge of salt and iron, he took Li's nephew Congzhi as administrative aide in charge of the Suzhou office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongying took charge of salt and iron, he appointed Li's nephew Congzhi as administrative aide in charge of the Suzhou office.

sentences.zh: 宰相令狐持不可，乃移書開諭，感悟，從之。

translations.literal: Chancellor Linghu Chi objected. Zhongying wrote a letter to enlighten and persuade him; Linghu was moved and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Linghu Chi disapproved, but Zhongying wrote to explain and persuade him; moved, Linghu gave way.

sentences.zh: 每私居內齋，束帶正色，服用簡素。

translations.literal: In private, even in his inner study at home, he wore his official sash and maintained a solemn demeanor; his attire was simple and plain.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the private study of his own home he wore his sash and kept a formal bearing, and his dress was always plain.

sentences.zh: 父子更九鎮，五為京兆，再為河南，皆不奏瑞，不度浮屠。

translations.literal: Father and son in succession held nine regional commands—five times as Jingzhao governor and twice as Henan governor—and none reported auspicious portents or had Buddhist rites performed.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son between them held nine regional commands: five terms as Jingzhao governor and two as Henan governor. None ever reported auspicious omens to the throne or patronized Buddhist salvation rites.

sentences.zh: 急於摘貪吏，濟單弱。

translations.literal: They were eager to remove corrupt officials and aid the weak and isolated.
translations.idiomatic: They were quick to purge greedy officials and to help the poor and defenseless.

sentences.zh: 每旱潦，必貸匱蠲負，裏無逋家。

translations.literal: Whenever drought or flood struck, they always loaned grain from stores, remitted debts, and left no household in the district in arrears.
translations.idiomatic: In every drought or flood they opened the granaries, canceled debts, and saw to it that no household in the district remained in default.

sentences.zh: 衣冠孤女不能自歸者，斥稟為婚嫁。

translations.literal: For orphaned daughters of genteel families who could not marry on their own, they allocated grain stipends for dowries.
