translations.idiomatic: Orphaned daughters of respectable families who lacked means to marry were given grain from the public stores for their weddings.

sentences.zh: 在朝，非慶吊不至宰相第。

translations.literal: While at court, except for celebrations or condolences they did not visit chancellors' residences.
translations.idiomatic: At court they never called at a chancellor's house except for weddings, funerals, and the like.

sentences.zh: 其跡略相同。

translations.literal: Their conduct was roughly the same.
translations.idiomatic: In these matters their ways were much alike.

sentences.zh: 家有書萬卷，所藏必三本：上者貯庫，其副常所閱，下者幼學焉。

translations.literal: The household owned ten thousand scrolls; every work was kept in three copies—the best stored in the library, a second for daily reading, and a third for the children's study.
translations.idiomatic: The family library held ten thousand scrolls, and every title was kept in triplicate: the finest copy went into the vault, a working copy stayed at hand for reading, and a third served the children's lessons.

sentences.zh: 仲郢嘗手鈔《六經》，司馬遷、班固、范曄史皆一鈔，魏晉及南北朝史再，又類所鈔它書凡三十篇，號《柳氏自備》；

translations.literal: Zhongying once hand-copied the Six Classics; the histories of Sima Qian, Ban Gu, and Fan Ye each once; the histories of Wei-Jin and the Northern and Southern Dynasties twice; and some thirty other copied works in all, entitled "The Liu Family's Self-Sufficiency";
translations.idiomatic: Zhongying once copied out the Six Classics by hand, each of the histories by Sima Qian, Ban Gu, and Fan Ye once, the Wei-Jin and Northern and Southern Dynasties histories twice, and some thirty other works besides—a collection he called The Liu Family's Self-Sufficiency;

sentences.zh: 旁錄仙佛書甚眾，皆楷小精真，無行字。

translations.literal: He also copied many Daoist and Buddhist works, all in small regular script, finely and faithfully rendered, with no running script.
translations.idiomatic: Alongside these he copied a great many Daoist and Buddhist texts, all in small, precise regular script—never a line of running hand.

sentences.zh: 子璞、珪、璧、玭。

translations.literal: His sons: Pu, Gui, Bi, and Pin.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Pu, Gui, Bi, and Pin.

sentences.zh: 子 璞

translations.literal: Son: Pu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Pu

sentences.zh: 璞，字韜玉，學不營仕。

translations.literal: Pu, courtesy name Taoyu, devoted himself to learning and did not seek office.
translations.idiomatic: Pu, styled Taoyu, pursued scholarship and never entered official life.

sentences.zh: 著《春秋三氏異同義》，又述《天祚長歷》，斷自漢武帝紀元，為編年，以大政、大祥異、侵叛戰伐隨著之，閏位者附見其左，常謂「杜征南《春秋後序》述紀甲歷為得實，自余史家皆差」，蔣系以為然。

translations.literal: He wrote "Differing Interpretations of the Three Commentators on the Spring and Autumn," and also compiled the "Long Calendar of Heavenly Blessing," beginning from Emperor Wu of Han's era designation as annals, recording major policies, major auspicious and strange omens, invasions, rebellions, wars, and campaigns as they occurred; usurpers were noted in the margin. He often said, "Du Yu's Postface to the Spring and Autumn, in describing the Jia-calendar chronology, got the facts right; all other historians are off." Jiang Xi agreed with him.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Differing Interpretations of the Three Commentators on the Spring and Autumn and also compiled the Long Calendar of Heavenly Blessing, starting from the inaugural year of Emperor Wu of Han as a chronicle in which great policies, great omens, invasions, rebellions, and campaigns were entered as they arose, with usurping regimes noted in the margin. He often remarked that Du Yu's Postface to the Spring and Autumn, in its account of the Jia-calendar chronology, had the facts right and that every other historian was wrong—and Jiang Xi agreed.

sentences.zh: 終著作郎。

translations.literal: He ended as Author-Editor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Author-Editor.

sentences.zh: 子 珪

translations.literal: Son: Gui
translations.idiomatic: Son: Gui

sentences.zh: 珪，字交玄。

translations.literal: Gui, courtesy name Jiaoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, styled Jiaoxuan.

sentences.zh: 大中中，與璧繼擢進士，皆秀整而文，杜牧、李商隱稱之。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era he and Bi in succession passed the jinshi examination; both were refined in bearing and literary, and Du Mu and Li Shangyin praised them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong reign they and Bi passed the jinshi examination in turn; both were handsome, polished, and literary, and Du Mu and Li Shangyin spoke highly of them.

sentences.zh: 杜悰鎮西川，表在幕府，久乃至。

translations.literal: When Du Cong governed Xichuan, he recommended Gui for his staff; Gui arrived only after a long delay.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Cong took command in Xichuan he had Gui appointed to his staff, but Gui did not arrive until long afterward.

sentences.zh: 會悰徙淮南，歸其積俸，珪不納，悰舉故事為言，卒辭之。

translations.literal: When Cong was transferred to Huainan, he returned Gui's accumulated salary; Gui would not accept it. Cong cited precedent, but Gui ultimately declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong was reassigned to Huainan he tried to return Gui's accumulated salary. Gui refused; Cong cited precedent, but in the end Gui would not take it.

sentences.zh: 以藍田尉直弘文館，遷右拾遺，而給事中蕭仿、鄭裔綽謂珪不能事父，封還其詔。

translations.literal: He was made Lantian county magistrate with concurrent duty at the Hongwen Library and promoted to Right Reminder, but the Palace Assistant Secretaries Xiao Fang and Zheng Yichuo said Gui could not serve his father properly and returned the edict unopened.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Lantian county magistrate with concurrent service at the Hongwen Library, he was promoted to Right Reminder, but the Palace Assistant Secretaries Xiao Fang and Zheng Yichuo declared that Gui was unable to care for his father and sent the appointment edict back unopened.

sentences.zh: 仲郢訴其子「冒處諫職為不可，謂不孝則誣。

translations.literal: Zhongying appealed on his son's behalf: "Holding a remonstrance office improperly is wrong, but to call him unfilial is slander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongying petitioned on his son's behalf: "It is wrong for him to hold a remonstrance post while his father still needs him, but to call him unfilial is a false charge.

sentences.zh: 請勒就養」，詔可。

translations.literal: Please order him to go home and support his parents." The edict was approved.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be ordered home to support his parents." The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 始，公綽治家埒韓滉，及珪被廢，士人愧悵。

translations.literal: At first Gongchuo's household management was on a par with Han Huang's; when Gui was dismissed, scholars felt shame and regret.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo's household had once been ranked with Han Huang's in good order; when Gui was removed from office, men of letters felt ashamed and dismayed.

sentences.zh: 終衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Minister of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Vice Minister of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 子 璧

translations.literal: Son: Bi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Bi

sentences.zh: 璧，字賓玉。

translations.literal: Bi, courtesy name Binyu.
translations.idiomatic: Bi, styled Binyu.

sentences.zh: 馬植鎮汴州，辟管書記。

translations.literal: When Ma Zhi governed Bianzhou, he recruited Bi as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Zhi was military governor of Bianzhou he took Bi on as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 又從李瓚桂州，規止其不法，瓚不聽，乃拂衣去。

translations.literal: Later he followed Li Zan to Guizhou, admonishing him to stop his illegal conduct; Zan would not listen, so he shook out his robes and left.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Li Zan in Guizhou and urged him to abandon his unlawful ways. When Zan refused to listen, Bi shook out his robes and walked away.

sentences.zh: 未幾，軍亂。

translations.literal: Before long the army mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward the army rose in mutiny.

sentences.zh: 擢右補闕，再轉屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Supplementation Censor and later transferred to become Assistant Director of the Bureau of State Farms.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Supplementation Censor and later moved to Assistant Director of the Bureau of State Farms.

sentences.zh: 僖宗幸蜀，授翰林學士，累遷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, Bi was made Hanlin Academician and was repeatedly promoted to Right Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong took refuge in Shu, Bi was appointed Hanlin Academician and rose in time to Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 子 玭

translations.literal: Son: Pin
translations.idiomatic: Son: Pin

sentences.zh: 玭以明經補秘書正字，由書判拔萃，累轉左補闕。

translations.literal: Pin passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Secretary Proofreader; through excellence in document review he was repeatedly promoted to Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the Mingjing examination, Pin was appointed Secretary Proofreader; distinguished in document review, he rose through several posts to Left Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 高湜再鎮昭義，皆表為副，擢刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Gao Chen twice governed Zhaoyi, he each time recommended Pin as his deputy, and Pin was promoted to Assistant Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Gao Chen took command of Zhaoyi he recommended Pin as his deputy, and Pin was promoted to Assistant Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 湜貶高要尉，比三疏申理。

translations.literal: When Chen was demoted to magistrate of Gaoyao, Pin submitted three memorials in succession pleading his case.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen was demoted to magistrate of Gaoyao, Pin submitted three memorials in a row in his defense.

sentences.zh: 湜後得稿嗟嘆，以為其言雖自辨不加也。

translations.literal: Later Chen obtained the draft and sighed in admiration, thinking that though the words were self-vindicating they were not excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Chen later obtained the draft and sighed over it, feeling that though Pin spoke in his own defense, he had not gone too far.

sentences.zh: 出為嶺南節度副使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as deputy military commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as deputy military commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 廨中橘熟，既食，乃納直於官。

translations.literal: When oranges in the yamen ripened, after eating them he paid their price into the official accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Oranges ripened in the yamen; after he ate some he paid their market price into the public coffers.

sentences.zh: 黃巢陷交、廣，逃還，除起居郎。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao captured Jiaozhi and Guangzhou, Pin fled back and was appointed Court Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao took Jiaozhi and Guangzhou, Pin escaped home and was appointed Court Diarist.

sentences.zh: 巢入京師，奔行在，再遷中書舍人、御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Chao entered the capital, Pin fled to the mobile court and was twice promoted to Secretariat Drafter and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao entered the capital, Pin fled to the emperor's camp and was promoted in turn to Secretariat Drafter and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 文德元年，以吏部侍郎脩國史，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wende he was made Vice Minister of Personnel to compile the national history and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wende he was made Vice Minister of Personnel with charge of the national history and appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 直清有父風，昭宗欲倚以相，中官譖比煩碎，非廊廟器，乃止。

translations.literal: Upright and pure, with his father's character, Emperor Zhaozong wished to rely on him as chancellor; eunuchs slandered that he was too fussy about details and not material for the highest office, so the plan stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and incorruptible in his father's mold, Pin was someone Emperor Zhaozong hoped to make chancellor, but eunuchs slandered him as finicky and petty—not timber for the grand hall—and the appointment went no further.

sentences.zh: 坐事貶瀘州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He was demoted to prefect of Luzhou on account of an offense and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted on a charge, he was demoted to prefect of Luzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 光化初，帝自華還，詔復官爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guanghua, when the emperor returned from Hua, an edict restored his offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guanghua, when the emperor returned from Hua, an edict restored Pin's rank and titles posthumously.

sentences.zh: 玭嘗述家訓以戒子孫曰：

translations.literal: Pin once set forth family instructions to warn his descendants, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Pin once laid down family instructions to admonish his descendants, saying:

sentences.zh: 夫門地高者，一事墜先訓，則異它人，雖生可以茍爵位，死不可見祖先地下。

translations.literal: For those of lofty lineage, if one thing falls from ancestral teachings, one differs from others; though in life one may scrape by with rank, in death one cannot face one's ancestors in the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: When one's gate is high, a single lapse from ancestral teaching sets one apart from other men: in life one may cling to rank by shameful means, but in death one cannot face one's forebears beneath the earth.

sentences.zh: 門高則自驕，族盛則人窺嫉。

translations.literal: High gates breed pride; flourishing clans draw envious eyes.
translations.idiomatic: A lofty gate invites pride; a flourishing clan invites jealous scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 實蓺懿行，人未必信；

translations.literal: Solid talent and virtuous conduct—people may not believe it;
translations.idiomatic: Real ability and fine conduct may not be believed;

sentences.zh: 纖瑕微累，十手爭指矣。

translations.literal: a tiny flaw or slight fault, and ten hands point at once.
translations.idiomatic: but the smallest blemish, and ten fingers point at once.

sentences.zh: 所以修己不得不至，為學不得不堅。

translations.literal: Therefore self-cultivation cannot but be thorough, and study cannot but be firm.
translations.idiomatic: That is why self-cultivation must be pushed to the limit and learning pursued without slackening.

sentences.zh: 夫士君子生於世，己無能而望它人用，己無善而望它人愛，猶農夫鹵莽種之而怨天澤不潤，雖欲弗餒，可乎？

translations.literal: A gentleman born into the world who lacks ability yet expects others to employ him, who lacks goodness yet expects others to love him, is like a farmer who plants carelessly and then blames heaven's grace for not moistening the fields—though he wish not to go hungry, can he?
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman in this world who has no talent yet expects others to use him, who has no virtue yet expects others to cherish him, is like a farmer who sows carelessly and then curses heaven for withholding rain: can he hope not to starve?

sentences.zh: 余幼聞先公仆射言：立己以孝悌為基，恭默為本，畏怯為務，勤儉為法。

translations.literal: In youth I heard my late father, the Pushe, say: establish yourself with filial piety and brotherly duty as foundation, reverent silence as root, cautious fear as task, and diligence and thrift as rule.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood I heard my late father, the Pushe, say: to stand as a man, take filial piety and brotherly duty as your foundation, reverent reserve as your base, prudent caution as your task, and diligence and thrift as your law.

sentences.zh: 肥家以忍順，保交以簡恭，廣記如不及，求名如儻來。

translations.literal: Enrich the family through forbearance and compliance, preserve friendships through simplicity and respect, record widely as if unable to keep up, and seek fame as if it came by chance.
translations.idiomatic: Enrich the household through patience and deference, keep friendships through plain courtesy, note everything as though you could never catch up, and treat fame as something that arrives unbidden.

sentences.zh: 蒞官則絜己省事，而後可以言家法；

translations.literal: When holding office, purify yourself and reduce affairs; only then may one speak of family law;
translations.idiomatic: In office, keep yourself clean and your business lean—only then may one speak of household discipline;

sentences.zh: 家法備，然後可以言養人。

translations.literal: when family law is complete, only then may one speak of nurturing others.
translations.idiomatic: when household discipline is complete, only then may one speak of raising others aright.

sentences.zh: 直不近禍，廉不沽名。

translations.literal: Integrity does not court calamity; purity does not trade for fame.
translations.idiomatic: Uprightness does not seek out disaster, and integrity does not haggle for a name.

sentences.zh: 憂與禍不偕，絜與富不並。

translations.literal: Care and calamity do not go together; purity and wealth do not coexist.
translations.idiomatic: Anxious care and calamity do not keep company; clean living and great wealth do not share a house.

sentences.zh: 董生有云：「吊者在門，賀者在閭。」

translations.literal: Master Dong said: "Mourners are at the gate, congratulators in the lane."
translations.idiomatic: Master Dong said: "When mourners stand at the gate and well-wishers in the lane,"

sentences.zh: 言憂則恐懼，恐懼則福至。

translations.literal: He meant that care brings fear, and fear brings blessing.
translations.idiomatic: he meant that worry breeds fear, and fear brings fortune.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「賀者在門，吊者在閭。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Congratulators are at the gate, mourners in the lane."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When well-wishers stand at the gate and mourners in the lane,"

sentences.zh: 言受福則驕奢，驕奢則禍至。

translations.literal: He meant that receiving blessing breeds arrogance and extravagance, and arrogance and extravagance bring calamity.
translations.idiomatic: he meant that receiving good fortune breeds pride and excess, and pride and excess bring disaster.

sentences.zh: 故世族遠長與命位豐約，不假問龜蓍星數，在處心行事而已。

translations.literal: Therefore whether a great clan endures far or perishes, whether rank and fortune are ample or meager, does not depend on tortoise shells, yarrow stalks, or star calculations—it lies in how one sets the mind and acts.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a great clan endures or dies out, whether rank and fortune wax or wane, does not depend on tortoise shells, yarrow stalks, or star lore—it depends only on how one thinks and acts.

sentences.zh: 昭國裏崔山南琯子孫之盛，仕族罕比。

translations.literal: The flourishing of the descendants of Cui Shannan of Zhaoguo Lane was rarely matched among official clans.
translations.idiomatic: Few official families could rival the prosperity of Cui Shannan's line in Zhaoguo Lane.

sentences.zh: 山南曾祖母長孫夫人年高無齒，祖母唐夫人事姑孝，每旦，櫛縰笄拜階下，升堂乳姑，長孫不粒食者數年。

translations.literal: Shannan's great-grandmother Lady Changsun was elderly and toothless. His grandmother Lady Tang served her mother-in-law filially; each dawn she would comb her hair, bind it, and perform the hairpin rite bowing on the steps, then ascend the hall and nurse her mother-in-law; Lady Changsun ate no grain for years.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan's great-grandmother, Lady Changsun, was old and had lost her teeth. His grandmother Lady Tang served her with perfect filial devotion: every morning she combed and bound her hair, performed the hairpin rite bowing on the steps, then went up to the hall and nursed her mother-in-law at the breast. For years Lady Changsun ate no grain at all.

sentences.zh: 一日病，言無以報吾婦，冀子孫皆得如婦孝。

translations.literal: One day she fell ill and said, "I have no way to repay my daughter-in-law; I hope all my descendants may be as filial as she."
translations.idiomatic: When she fell ill one day she said, "I can never repay my daughter-in-law; may all my descendants be as filial as she is."

sentences.zh: 然則崔之門安得不大乎？

translations.literal: How then could the gate of the Cui clan fail to be great?
translations.idiomatic: How then could the house of Cui fail to flourish?

sentences.zh: 東都仁和裏裴尚書寬子孫眾盛，實為名閥。

translations.literal: The descendants of Vice Minister Pei Kuan of Renhe Lane in the Eastern Capital were numerous and flourishing—a true eminent clan.
translations.idiomatic: The descendants of Vice Minister Pei Kuan of Renhe Lane in Luoyang were many and thriving—a true great house.

sentences.zh: 天後時，宰相魏玄同選尚書之先為婿，未成婚而魏陷羅織獄，家徙嶺表。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time Chancellor Wei Xuantong chose the Vice Minister's daughter as betrothed for his son; before the marriage Wei was caught in a fabricated case and the family was exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, Chancellor Wei Xuantong betrothed his son to the Vice Minister's daughter, but before the wedding Wei was trapped in a fabricated charge and the family was banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 及北還，女已逾笄。

translations.literal: When they returned north, the girl had already passed the age of pinning up her hair.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned north, the girl was already past marriageable age.

sentences.zh: 其家議無以為衣食資，願下發為尼。

translations.literal: Her family discussed that they had no means of livelihood and wished to have her take the tonsure as a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Her family debated what they could live on and proposed that she be tonsured as a nun.

sentences.zh: 有一尼自外至，曰：「女福厚豐，必有令匹，子孫將遍天下，宜北歸。」

translations.literal: A nun came from outside and said, "The girl's fortune is deep and ample; she will surely have a worthy match, and her descendants will spread throughout the realm. She should return north."
translations.idiomatic: A nun arrived from outside and said, "This girl's blessing is great; she will surely find a worthy husband, and her descendants will fill the realm. She ought to return north."

sentences.zh: 家人遂不敢議。

translations.literal: The family then dared not discuss it further.
translations.idiomatic: At that the family dared raise the matter no further.

sentences.zh: 及荊門，則裴賫裝以迎矣。

translations.literal: When they reached Jingmen, Pei had loaded gifts to welcome her.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Jingmen, Pei was already there with a train of gifts to welcome her.

sentences.zh: 今勢利之徒，舍信誓如返掌，則裴之蕃衍，乃天之報施也。

translations.literal: Today's men of power and profit cast sworn faith aside as easily as turning the palm; then the spread of the Pei clan was heaven's reward.
translations.idiomatic: Men of power today discard sworn faith as easily as turning the hand; the Pei clan's flourishing was heaven's recompense for keeping theirs.

sentences.zh: 余舊府高公先君兄弟三人，俱居清列，非速客不二羹胾，夕食，龁卜瓠而已，皆保重名於世。

translations.literal: My former superior Gao's father and his three brothers all held pure offices; unless a sudden guest came they never served two meat dishes, and for the evening meal they gnawed only pickled gourd—each guarding a weighty reputation in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The father of my former chief Gao and his three brothers all held high clean offices; unless an unexpected guest arrived they never set out more than one meat dish, and for supper they ate only pickled gourd—each guarding a hard-won name in the world.

sentences.zh: 永寧王相國涯居位，竇氏女歸，請曰：「玉工貨釵直七十萬錢。」

translations.literal: When Wang Ya, Prince of Yongning and chancellor, was in office, his daughter Dou returned home and asked, "A jade craftsman is selling a hairpin for seven hundred thousand cash."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ya, Prince of Yongning, was chancellor, his daughter Dou came home and asked, "A jade craftsman is offering a hairpin for seven hundred thousand cash."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「七十萬錢，豈於女惜？

translations.literal: Wang said, "Seven hundred thousand cash—would I begrudge that for my daughter?
translations.idiomatic: Wang said, "Seven hundred thousand cash—is that something I would begrudge my daughter?

sentences.zh: 但釵直若此，乃妖物也，禍必隨之。」

translations.literal: But if a hairpin costs so much, it is an evil object; calamity is sure to follow."
translations.idiomatic: But a hairpin that costs so much is an uncanny thing—disaster is sure to follow it."

sentences.zh: 女不復敢言。

translations.literal: The daughter no longer dared speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: After that the daughter did not dare mention it again.

sentences.zh: 後釵為馮球外郎妻首飾，涯曰：「為郎吏妻，首飾有七十萬錢，其可久乎！」

translations.literal: Later the hairpin became the headdress of the wife of Feng Qiu, an outer-office official. Ya said, "As the wife of a low-ranking clerk, to wear a headdress worth seven hundred thousand cash—can that last long!"
translations.idiomatic: Later the hairpin turned up as the headdress of Feng Qiu's wife, a clerk in the outer offices. Ya said, "For a clerk's wife to wear a seven-hundred-thousand-cash ornament—how can that end well?"

sentences.zh: 馮為賈相國餗門人，賈有奴頗橫，馮愛賈，召奴責之，奴泣謝。

translations.literal: Feng was a follower of Chancellor Jia Su. Jia had a slave who was quite overbearing; Feng, out of regard for Jia, summoned the slave and rebuked him; the slave wept and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was a client of Chancellor Jia Su. Jia had a slave who bullied others; out of loyalty to Jia, Feng summoned the slave and scolded him, and the slave wept and apologized.

sentences.zh: 未幾，馮晨謁賈，賈未出，有二青衣賫銀罌出，曰：「公恐君寒，奉地黃酒三杯。」

translations.literal: Before long, one morning Feng called on Jia; Jia had not yet come out when two green-robed attendants brought out a silver jar and said, "The lord fears you are cold and sends three cups of rehmannia wine."
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, Feng called on Jia one morning. Jia had not yet appeared when two green-robed attendants came out with a silver jar and said, "My lord fears you are cold and sends three cups of rehmannia wine."

sentences.zh: 馮悅，盡舉之。

translations.literal: Feng was pleased and drained them all.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Feng drank them down to the last drop.

sentences.zh: 俄病渴且咽，因暴卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was stricken with thirst and choking and suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was seized by burning thirst and choking, and died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 賈為嘆息出涕，卒不知其由。

translations.literal: Jia sighed and shed tears, never learning the cause to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Jia sighed and wept, but never learned what had killed him.

sentences.zh: 明年，王、賈皆遘禍。

translations.literal: The next year both Wang and Jia met with calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The following year both Wang and Jia met disaster.

sentences.zh: 噫，王以珍玩為物之妖，信知言矣，而不知恩權隆赫之妖甚於物邪？

translations.literal: Alas! Wang took precious curios as the evil in things—he truly knew what he was saying—yet did he not see that the evil of favor, power, and towering eminence is greater than that of objects?
translations.idiomatic: Alas! Wang was right to call precious trinkets uncanny things—but did he not see that the uncanny power of favor and towering authority is worse than any object?

sentences.zh: 馮以卑位貪貨，不能正其家，忠於所事，不能保其身，不足言矣。

translations.literal: Feng, in a low station yet greedy for goods, could not set his household aright; loyal to his patron, he could not preserve his own life—not worth speaking of.
translations.idiomatic: Feng, low in rank yet greedy for finery, could not govern his household; loyal to his patron, he could not save his own life—hardly worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 賈之奴害客於墻廡間而不知，欲始終富貴，其得乎？

translations.literal: Jia's slave harmed a guest in the corridor without his knowing—could he hope to remain rich and honored to the end?
translations.idiomatic: Jia's slave murdered a guest in the side hall without his master ever knowing—could such a man hope to die rich and honored?

sentences.zh: 舒相國元輿與李繁有隙，為御史，鞫譙獄，窮致繁罪，後舒亦及禍。

translations.literal: Chancellor Shu Yuanyu had a grudge against Li Fan; as censor he tried the Qiao case and pressed Fan's guilt to the limit; later Shu also met with calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Shu Yuanyu bore a grudge against Li Fan; as censor he tried the Qiao case and hounded Fan to conviction—and later Shu met disaster himself.

sentences.zh: 今世人盛言宿業報應，曾不思視履考祥事歟？

translations.literal: People today loudly proclaim karma from past lives and retribution—do they never think to examine their conduct and consider auspicious signs?
translations.idiomatic: People today love to talk of karma and retribution from past lives—have they never thought to examine their own conduct and read the omens in it?

sentences.zh: 夫名門右族，莫不由祖考忠孝勤儉以成立之，莫不由子孫頑率奢傲以覆墜之。

translations.literal: Great gates and eminent clans are all established by ancestors' loyalty, filial piety, diligence, and thrift, and all overthrown by descendants' obstinacy, extravagance, and arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Great houses are built by forebears through loyalty, filial piety, diligence, and thrift, and cast down by descendants through stubbornness, extravagance, and pride.

sentences.zh: 成立之難如升天，覆墜之易如燎毛。

translations.literal: To establish them is as hard as ascending heaven; to overthrow them as easy as singeing hair.
translations.idiomatic: To build them up is as hard as climbing to heaven; to ruin them as easy as setting fire to dry grass.

sentences.zh: 余家本以學識禮法稱於士林，比見諸家於吉兇禮制有疑者，多取正焉。

translations.literal: Our family was originally famed among scholars for learning, knowledge, and ritual propriety; lately when other families had doubts about auspicious and inauspicious rites, many sought correction from us.
translations.idiomatic: Our house was once known among scholars for learning and ritual propriety; whenever other families were uncertain about rites of mourning and celebration, they often came to us for guidance.

sentences.zh: 喪亂以來，門祚衰落，基構之重，屬於後生。

translations.literal: Since the disorders, the family's fortune has declined; the weight of the foundation falls on the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: Since the rebellions our line has waned; the burden of the foundation now rests on the young.

sentences.zh: 夫行道之人，德行文學為根株，正直剛毅為柯葉。

translations.literal: For one who walks the Way, virtue and literary learning are root and trunk; uprightness and firm resolve are branch and leaf.
translations.idiomatic: For one who would live rightly, moral character and learning are the root and trunk; integrity and steadfastness are the branches and leaves.

sentences.zh: 有根無葉，或可俟時；

translations.literal: With root but no leaf, one may perhaps wait for the season;
translations.idiomatic: With roots but no leaves, one may yet wait for the season;

sentences.zh: 有葉無根，膏雨所不能活也。

translations.literal: with leaf but no root, even nourishing rain cannot keep it alive.
translations.idiomatic: but with leaves and no root, even the kindest rain cannot keep the tree alive.

sentences.zh: 至於孝慈、友悌、忠信、篤行，乃食之醢醬，可一日無哉？

translations.literal: As for filial piety, kindness, brotherly harmony, loyalty, faith, and earnest conduct—these are the relish and sauce of food; can one go a day without them?
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety, kindness, brotherly duty, loyalty, faith, and earnest conduct are the salt and sauce of life—can one do without them for a single day?

sentences.zh: 其大概如此。

translations.literal: The general outline is thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the general outline.

sentences.zh: 弟 公權

translations.literal: Younger brother: Gongquan
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Gongquan

sentences.zh: 公權，字誠懸，公綽弟也。

translations.literal: Gongquan, courtesy name Chengxuan, was Gongchuo's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongquan, whose courtesy name was Chengxuan, was the younger brother of Liu Gongchuo.

sentences.zh: 年十二，工辭賦。

translations.literal: At age twelve he was skilled at prose-poems.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he already excelled at rhymed prose.

sentences.zh: 元和初，擢進士第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he was promoted to the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuanhe period he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 李聽鎮夏州，表為掌書記。

translations.literal: Li Ting governed Xiazhou and memorialized the throne to appoint him as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ting served as military governor of Xiazhou, he nominated Gongquan as his secretary.

sentences.zh: 因入奏，穆宗曰：「朕嘗於佛廟見卿筆跡，思之久矣。」

translations.literal: Because he entered the capital to report, Muzong said: "I once saw your calligraphy in a Buddhist temple and have long thought of you."
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court to report, Emperor Muzong said, "I once saw your handwriting in a Buddhist temple and have missed you ever since."

sentences.zh: 即拜右拾遺、侍書學士，再遷司封員外郎。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed Right Reminder and Palace Calligraphy Scholar, and was later transferred to be Vice-Director of the Department of Titles.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately made Right Reminder and Palace Calligraphy Scholar, and soon promoted to Vice-Director in the Department of Titles.

sentences.zh: 帝問公權用筆法，對曰：「心正則筆正，筆正乃可法矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Gongquan about his brush method; he replied: "When the heart is upright, then the brush is upright; only when the brush is upright can it serve as a model."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about his brushwork. Gongquan answered, "When the mind is upright, the brush is upright—and only an upright brush can serve as a model."

sentences.zh: 時帝荒縱，故公權及之。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was dissolute and unrestrained, so Gongquan touched on this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then given to indulgence, and Gongquan was admonishing him through his brush.

sentences.zh: 帝改容，悟其以筆諫也。

translations.literal: The emperor changed his expression, understanding that he was admonishing through calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face changed as he grasped that Gongquan was remonstrating through calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 公綽嘗寓書宰相李宗閔，言家弟本誌儒學，先朝以侍書見用，頗類工祝，願徙散秩。

translations.literal: Gongchuo once sent a letter to the chief minister Li Zongmin, saying his younger brother originally aspired to Confucian learning; the former court employed him for attendant writing, which was rather like the work of artisan priests, and he wished to be transferred to a less prestigious post.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo once wrote to Chief Minister Li Zongmin that his younger brother had set his heart on Confucian learning, yet the previous court had used him mainly as a palace calligrapher—a role too much like a temple scribe—and asked that he be moved to an ordinary post.

sentences.zh: 乃改右司郎中、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: He was therefore changed to Right Section Director and Scholar of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly reassigned as Right Section Director and a scholar of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 文宗復召侍書，遷中書舍人，充翰林書詔學士。

translations.literal: Wenzong again summoned him for attendant writing and promoted him to Secretariat Drafter, serving as Hanlin Calligraphy and Edict Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong recalled him as palace calligrapher and made him Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin Edict-and-Calligraphy Scholar.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜召對子亭，燭窮而語未盡，宮人以蠟液濡紙繼之。

translations.literal: Once at night he was summoned to audience at Ziting Pavilion; the candles were exhausted before the conversation ended, so palace women moistened paper with wax to extend them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor summoned him at night to Ziting Pavilion; the candles burned down before they had finished speaking, and palace women dipped paper in wax to keep the light going.

sentences.zh: 從幸未央宮，帝駐輦，曰：「朕有一喜，邊戍賜衣久不時，今中春而衣已給。」

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on a visit to Weiyang Palace, the emperor halted his carriage and said: "I have one cause for joy: for long the border garrisons' gift-clothing has not arrived on time; now at mid-spring the garments have already been distributed."
translations.idiomatic: On an outing to Weiyang Palace, the emperor halted his carriage and said, "I have good news: border garrisons have long received their seasonal clothing late, but this year by mid-spring the issue is already complete."

sentences.zh: 公權為數十言稱賀，帝曰：「當賀我以詩。」

translations.literal: Gongquan offered several dozen words of congratulation; the emperor said: "You should congratulate me with a poem."
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan spoke a few dozen words of congratulation. The emperor said, "Congratulate me in verse instead."

sentences.zh: 宮人迫之，公權應聲成，文婉切而麗。

translations.literal: Palace women pressed him; Gongquan composed it on the spot, the wording refined, earnest, and graceful.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants pressed him; Gongquan answered at once, his lines tender, apt, and beautifully wrought.

sentences.zh: 詔令再賦，復無停思，天子甚悅，曰：「子建七步，爾乃三焉。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to compose again; once more without pause for thought, the Son of Heaven was greatly pleased and said: "Zijian needed seven paces; you need only three."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered another poem; again Gongquan composed without hesitation. Delighted, the Son of Heaven said, "Cao Zijian needed seven steps—you need only three."

sentences.zh: 常與六學士對便殿，帝稱漢文帝恭儉，因舉袂曰：「此三澣矣！」

translations.literal: He often joined the six scholars in audience at the Convenient Hall; the emperor praised Emperor Wen of Han for respect and thrift, and raising his sleeve said: "This has been washed three times!"
translations.idiomatic: He often met with the six Hanlin scholars in the side hall. Praising Emperor Wen of Han for modest thrift, the emperor lifted his sleeve and said, "I've washed this three times already!"

sentences.zh: 學士皆賀，獨公權無言。

translations.literal: All the scholars congratulated him, but Gongquan alone said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The scholars all offered congratulations; only Gongquan remained silent.

sentences.zh: 帝問之，對曰：「人主當進賢退不肖，納諫諍，明賞罰。

translations.literal: The emperor asked him about it; he replied: "The ruler ought to advance the worthy and dismiss the unworthy, accept remonstrance, and make rewards and punishments clear.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked why, he answered, "A ruler should promote the worthy and remove the unfit, heed remonstrance, and make rewards and punishments clear.

sentences.zh: 服澣濯之衣，此小節耳，非有益治道者。」

translations.literal: Wearing clothes washed again and again is but a small matter and not what benefits the way of governance."
translations.idiomatic: Wearing a thrice-washed robe is a trifle; it is not what truly benefits good government."

sentences.zh: 異日，與周墀同對，論事不阿，墀為惴恐，公權益不奪，帝徐曰：「卿有諍臣風，可屈居諫議大夫。」

translations.literal: On another day, together with Zhou Chi he answered at audience; in discussing affairs he did not yield, Zhou Chi was fearful on his behalf, but Gongquan was all the more unwavering; the emperor said slowly: "You have the manner of a remonstrating minister; you may acceptably take the lower rank of Remonstrance Grandee."
translations.idiomatic: On another day he and Zhou Chi were in audience together. Gongquan spoke without flattery on policy; Zhou Chi quaked with fear, but Gongquan only grew firmer. The emperor said at length, "You have the spirit of a remonstrating minister. You may acceptably step down to Remonstrance Grandee."

sentences.zh: 乃自舍人下遷，仍為學士知制誥。

translations.literal: He was therefore demoted from drafter, yet remained a scholar drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: So he was demoted from Secretariat Drafter, but kept his duties as a Hanlin scholar drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，轉工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng he was transferred to Vice-Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 3 (838) he was made Vice-Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 召問得失，因言：「郭文領邠寧，而議者頗有臧否。」

translations.literal: Summoned and asked about gain and loss, he therefore said: "Guo Wen commands Binning, and critics have both praise and blame."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to discuss what was going wrong, he said, "Guo Wen holds Binning, and opinion about him is sharply divided."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「文，尚父從子，太皇太后季父，官無玷郵，自大金吾位方鎮，何所更議？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wen is the Grand Preceptor's nephew and the Grand Empress Dowager's uncle; his office bears no stain; from Grand Gold Crow Guard to a frontier command—what more is there to discuss?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wen is the Grand Preceptor's nephew and the Grand Empress Dowager's uncle. His record is spotless, and he rose from the Grand Gold Crow Guard to a frontier command—what is left to criticize?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「文誠勛舊，然人謂獻二女乃有是除，信乎？」

translations.literal: He replied: "Wen is indeed an old meritorious servant, yet people say he received this appointment for presenting two daughters—is it true?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Guo Wen is indeed a veteran of merit, but people say this appointment came from offering two daughters to the palace—is that true?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「女自參承太后，豈獻哉？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The daughters themselves attended and served the empress dowager—how can that be called presenting them?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Those girls entered the palace to serve the empress dowager directly—how is that an offering?"

sentences.zh: 公權曰：「疑嫌間不可戶曉。」

translations.literal: Gongquan said: "Suspicion and doubt cannot be explained household by household."
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan said, "Once suspicion arises, you cannot make every household understand."

sentences.zh: 因引王珪諫廬江王妃事。

translations.literal: He therefore cited Wang Gui's remonstrance regarding the Princess of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He then cited Wang Gui's remonstrance in the matter of the Princess of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝命中官自南內送女還文家。

translations.literal: That same day the emperor ordered a eunuch from the Southern Inner Palace to send the daughters back to Wen's family.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the emperor ordered a palace eunuch to return the daughters from the Southern Inner Court to the Wen household.

sentences.zh: 其忠益多類此。

translations.literal: His loyal counsel was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his loyal remonstrances were like this.

sentences.zh: 遷學士承旨。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Senior Hanlin Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Senior Scholar of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，罷為右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Wuzong acceded, he was dismissed to be Right Regular Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Gongquan was removed and made Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔珙引為集賢院學士，知院事。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Cui Gong recommended him as Scholar of the Jixian Academy and charged him with directing its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Cui Gong had him appointed Jixian Academy scholar and put him in charge of the institute.

sentences.zh: 李德裕不悅，左授太子詹事，改賓客。

translations.literal: Li Deyu was displeased and transferred him leftward to be Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then changed to Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu was displeased and demoted him to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, later making him Guest of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 累封河東郡公，復為常侍，進至太子少師。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Hedong, restored as Regular Attendant, and advanced to Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Hedong, restored as Regular Attendant, and eventually rose to Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 大中十三年，天子元會，公權稍耄忘，先群臣稱賀，占奏忽謬，御史劾之，奪一季俸，議者恨其不歸事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dazhong, at the emperor's New Year's audience, Gongquan, somewhat senile and forgetful, before all the officials offered congratulations; his prognostic memorial suddenly had errors; censors impeached him and he was deprived of one season's salary; critics regretted that he did not retire.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong 13, at the New Year's audience Gongquan, now somewhat senile, congratulated the emperor ahead of the other officials but bungled his auspicious memorial. Censors impeached him and his salary was docked for a season; many wished he had retired instead.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，乃以太子太保致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he retired with the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xiantong period he retired as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十八。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太師。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 公權博貫經術，於《詩》、《書》、《左氏春秋》、《國語》、莊周書尤邃，每解一義，必數十百言。

translations.literal: Gongquan was broadly versed in the classics; he was especially deep in the Book of Songs, Book of Documents, Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals, Discourses of the States, and the writings of Zhuang Zhou; whenever he explained one meaning he invariably spoke several tens or hundreds of words.
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan was deeply read in the classics, especially the Book of Songs, the Book of Documents, the Zuo Commentary, the Discourses of the States, and Zhuangzi; whenever he expounded a single point he would speak at great length.

sentences.zh: 通音律，而不喜奏樂，曰：「聞之令人驕怠。」

translations.literal: He understood music but did not like to have it performed, saying: "Hearing it makes one arrogant and slack."
translations.idiomatic: He understood music theory but disliked hearing performances, saying, "Music makes people proud and lazy."

sentences.zh: 其書法結體勁媚，自成一家。

translations.literal: His calligraphy in structure combined strength and grace, forming a school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy united vigor and elegance in a style entirely his own.

sentences.zh: 文宗嘗召與聯句，帝曰：「人皆苦炎熱，我愛夏日長。」

translations.literal: Wenzong once summoned him for linked verses; the emperor said: "All men suffer from scorching heat; I love the long summer days."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong once invited him to compose linked verses. The emperor opened: "All men brood on sweltering heat; I love how long the summer days are."

sentences.zh: 公權屬曰：「薰風自南來，殿閣生餘涼。」

translations.literal: Gongquan continued: "The fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions breathe lingering coolness."
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan answered: "A sweet wind blows from the south; the palace halls fill with lingering cool."

sentences.zh: 它學士亦屬繼，帝獨諷公權者，以為詞情皆足，命題於殿壁，字率徑五寸，帝嘆曰：「鐘、王無以尚也！」

translations.literal: Other scholars also continued in turn; the emperor recited Gongquan's alone, deeming both wording and feeling complete, and ordered the lines written on the hall wall, each character about five inches across; the emperor sighed: "Zhong and Wang cannot be surpassed!"
translations.idiomatic: Other scholars added lines as well, but the emperor recited only Gongquan's, finding both words and feeling faultless. He had the couplet brushed on the hall wall in characters five inches high and marveled, "Not even Zhong You or Wang Xizhi can match this!"

sentences.zh: 其遷少師，宣宗召至禦座前，書紙三番，作真、行、草三體，奇秘，賜以器幣，且詔自書謝章，無限真、行。

translations.literal: When he was promoted to Junior Preceptor, Xuanzong summoned him before the imperial seat; he wrote paper three times, producing regular, running, and cursive scripts, wondrous and rare; he was granted vessels and silks, and also ordered to write his own thank-you memorial in no fixed limit of regular or running script.
translations.idiomatic: When he was made Junior Preceptor, Emperor Xuanzong summoned him before the throne. Gongquan wrote out three sheets in regular, running, and cursive script—work so marvelous the court had rarely seen its like. The emperor bestowed gifts and ordered him to write his own memorial of thanks in whatever script he chose.

sentences.zh: 當時大臣家碑誌，非其筆，人以子孫為不孝。

translations.literal: At the time for stele inscriptions and epitaphs in great ministers' families, if not in his hand people regarded their descendants as unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, epitaphs and steles for great ministers' families that were not in his hand were taken as proof their descendants lacked filial piety.

sentences.zh: 外夷入貢者，皆別署貨貝曰：「此購柳書。」

translations.literal: Foreign tribesmen who came bearing tribute all separately set aside goods marked: "This is for purchasing Liu's calligraphy."
translations.idiomatic: Tributary envoys from abroad set aside part of their goods marked, "For purchasing Liu's calligraphy."

sentences.zh: 嘗書京兆西明寺《金剛經》，有鐘、王、歐、虞、褚、陸諸家法，自為得意。

translations.literal: He once wrote the Diamond Sutra for Ximing Temple in Jingzhao, incorporating the methods of the Zhong, Wang, Ouyang, Yu, Chu, and Lu schools; he considered it his own finest work.
translations.idiomatic: He once copied the Diamond Sutra for Ximing Temple in the capital, drawing on the styles of Zhong, Wang, Ouyang, Yu, Chu, and Lu—and counted it his proudest work.

sentences.zh: 凡公卿以書貺遺，蓋巨萬，而主藏奴或盜用。

translations.literal: In all, great officials presented calligraphy gifts to him amounting to tens of thousands, yet the chief storekeeper slave sometimes embezzled them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials showered him with calligraphic gifts worth tens of thousands of strings of cash, but his head steward would sometimes steal from them.

sentences.zh: 嘗貯杯盂一笥，縢識如故而器皆亡，奴妄言叵測者，公權笑曰：「銀杯羽化矣！」

translations.literal: Once he stored cups and bowls in one basket; the binding labels remained as before but the vessels were all gone; the slave spoke wildly of the unknowable; Gongquan laughed and said: "The silver cups have ascended as immortals!"
translations.idiomatic: Once he stored a basket of cups and bowls; the wax seals were intact but every vessel was gone. When the slave babbled about uncanny causes, Gongquan only laughed and said, "My silver cups have achieved transcendence!"

sentences.zh: 不復詰。

translations.literal: He did not press further.
translations.idiomatic: He asked no more.

sentences.zh: 唯研、筆、圖籍，自鐍秘之。

translations.literal: Only inkstones, brushes, books, and maps he locked and kept secret himself.
translations.idiomatic: Only his inkstones, brushes, and books he kept under lock himself.

sentences.zh: 諸父 子華

translations.literal: Paternal uncle: Zihua
translations.idiomatic: Paternal uncle: Zihua

sentences.zh: 子華，公綽諸父也。

translations.literal: Zihua was Gongchuo's paternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Zihua was Liu Gongchuo's uncle.

sentences.zh: 始辟嚴武劍南府，累遷池州刺史。

translations.literal: He was first recruited to Yan Wu's Sword-South staff and was promoted in succession to Prefect of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered Yan Wu's staff in Jiannan and eventually rose to prefect of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 代宗將幸華清宮，先命完葺，欲以子華為京兆少尹，尹惡其剛方，沮解之，遂為昭應令、檢校金部郎中、修宮使。

translations.literal: When Daizong was about to visit Huaqing Palace he first ordered repairs completed; he wished to make Zihua Junior Administrator of Jingzhao; the Administrator disliked his stern uprightness and obstructed and dissolved the appointment; he therefore became Magistrate of Zhaoying, Acting Director of the Department of Gold, and Palace Repair Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong planned a visit to Huaqing Palace and ordered the grounds rebuilt, he meant to make Zihua Junior Administrator of Jingzhao. The chief administrator resented his uncompromising manner and blocked the appointment, so Zihua became magistrate of Zhaoying, acting director in the Department of Gold, and commissioner overseeing the palace repairs.

sentences.zh: 設棘圍於市，徇邑中曰：「民有得華清瓦石材用，投圍中，逾三日不還者死。」

translations.literal: He set up a thorn fence enclosure in the market and proclaimed through the district: "If any commoner finds Huaqing tiles or stone useful, throw them into the enclosure; whoever does not return them within three days dies."
translations.idiomatic: He erected a thorn-fenced enclosure in the market and proclaimed through the district, "Anyone who finds usable tile or stone from Huaqing must deposit it here; failure to do so within three days is punishable by death."

sentences.zh: 不終日，已山積矣，營辦略足。

translations.literal: Before the day ended they were heaped like a mountain; the preparations were nearly sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Before the day was out the pile stood like a hill, and the work was nearly complete.

sentences.zh: 宰相元載有別墅，以奴主務，自稱郎將，怙勢縱暴，租賦未嘗入官。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Yuan Zai had a villa; a slave managed its affairs, styled himself Commandant, relied on power and indulged in violence, and rent and tax never entered the government.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Yuan Zai owned a villa run by a slave who styled himself a commandant, abused his master's power, and never forwarded rent or tax to the state.

sentences.zh: 子華因奴入謁，收付獄，劾發宿罪，杖殺之，一邑震伏。

translations.literal: When the slave entered to pay respects, Zihua seized him, handed him to prison, impeached and exposed old crimes, beat him to death, and the whole district was awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: When the slave came to pay court, Zihua had him arrested, dredged up old crimes, and flogged him to death—the whole district trembled into obedience.

sentences.zh: 載不敢怨，遣吏厚謝。

translations.literal: Zai did not dare resent it and sent an official with generous thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai dared not complain and sent an official with lavish thanks.

sentences.zh: 預知其終，自為墓銘。

translations.literal: Foreknowing his end he wrote his own tomb epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: Foreknowing his death, he wrote his own tomb inscription.

sentences.zh: 子公器、公度。

translations.literal: Sons: Gongqi and Gongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Sons: Gongqi and Gongdu.

sentences.zh: 公度善攝生，年八十餘，有強力。

translations.literal: Gongdu was skilled at nourishing life; in his eighties he still had great strength.
translations.idiomatic: Gongdu mastered the art of preserving health; past eighty he still had great strength.

sentences.zh: 常云：「吾初無術，但未嘗以氣海暖冷物，熟生物，不以元氣佐喜怒耳。」

translations.literal: He often said: "I originally had no special method, but I never used warming or cooling things on the sea of qi, never ate uncooked food, and never used my primordial qi to fuel anger or joy."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "I never had any secret art—only this: I never sent hot or cold things into my belly, never ate raw food, and never let joy or anger consume my vital energy."

sentences.zh: 位光祿少卿。

translations.literal: He served as Vice-Director of the Directorate of Banquets.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice-Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 公器生遵，遵生燦，別有傳。

translations.literal: Gongqi begat Zun; Zun begat Can; each has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Gongqi's son was Zun; Zun's son was Can—they receive separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 楊於陵

translations.literal: Yang Yuling
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuling

sentences.zh: 楊於陵，字達夫，本漢太尉震之裔。

translations.literal: Yang Yuling, courtesy name Dafu, was originally a descendant of the Han Grand Commandant Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuling, courtesy name Dafu, traced his line to Zhen, Grand Commandant of Han.

sentences.zh: 父太清，倦宦，客河朔，死安祿山之亂。

translations.literal: His father Taiqing, weary of office, sojourned in the north of the Yellow River and died in the An Lushan rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: His father Taiqing, weary of official life, lived as a guest north of the Yellow River and died in the An Lushan rebellion.

sentences.zh: 於陵始六歲，間關至江左，逮長，有奇誌。

translations.literal: Yuling was only six when he made his perilous way to the lands east of the Yangtze; when he grew up he had extraordinary aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: Yuling was only six when he made the hard journey south of the Yangtze; grown to manhood, he harbored uncommon ambitions.

sentences.zh: 十八擢進士，調句容主簿。

translations.literal: At eighteen he was promoted to jinshi and was assigned as Recorder of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he passed the jinshi examination and was posted as recorder in Jurong.

sentences.zh: 節度使韓滉剛嚴少許可，獨奇於陵，謂妻柳曰：「吾求佳婿，無如於陵賢。」

translations.literal: Military Governor Han Huang was stern and strict and rarely approved anyone; he alone marveled at Yuling and said to his wife Liu: "In seeking a fine son-in-law, none is so worthy as Yuling."
translations.idiomatic: The military governor Han Huang was stern and sparing of praise, yet he singled out Yuling and told his wife, Lady Liu, "In all my search for a son-in-law, none matches Yuling."

sentences.zh: 因以妻之。

translations.literal: He therefore gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 辟鄂嶽、江西使府。

translations.literal: He was recruited to the E-Yue and Jiangxi commissioners' staffs.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the staff of the E-Yue and Jiangxi commissioners.

sentences.zh: 滉居宰相，領財賦，權震中外。

translations.literal: Huang served as chief minister and oversaw revenues; his power shook court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Huang became chief minister and controlled the treasury, his power eclipsed court and realm alike.

sentences.zh: 於陵隨府罷，避親不肯調，退廬建昌，以文書自娛樂。

translations.literal: When Yuling's staff appointment ended with the office's dissolution, he avoided nepotism and refused reassignment, retiring to Jianchang in Lushan and amusing himself with documents.
translations.idiomatic: When his post ended with Han Huang's staff, Yuling declined reassignment to avoid favoritism, withdrew to Jianchang in Mount Lu, and devoted himself to letters.

sentences.zh: 滉卒，乃入為膳部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Huang died he then entered service as Vice-Director of the Department of Food.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Huang died, he entered court as Vice-Director in the Department of Food.

sentences.zh: 以吏部判南曹，選者恃與宰相親，文書不如式，於陵駁其違，宰相怒，以南曹郎出使吊宣武軍。

translations.literal: As Vice-Minister of Personnel he judged the Southern Bureau; a selectee relied on kinship with the chief minister and his documents did not conform to form; Yuling rejected the violation; the chief minister was angry and sent the Southern Bureau director as envoy to condole the Xuanwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: While judging appointments in the Ministry of Personnel's Southern Bureau, Yuling rejected a candidate's irregular paperwork—the man had counted on kinship with the chief minister. The minister was furious and shunted Yuling out as condolence envoy to the Xuanwu army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷右司郎中，換吏部，出為絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Right Section Director, exchanged to the Ministry of Personnel, and went out as Prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Right Section Director, then moved within the Ministry of Personnel, and was sent out as prefect of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德宗雅聞其名，留拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: Dezong had long heard his name and retained him, appointing him Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong had long heard of him and kept him at court as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 時京兆李實恃恩暴橫，於陵與所善許孟容不離附，為所譖短，徙秘書少監。

translations.literal: At the time Li Shi of Jingzhao relied on favor and was violent and overbearing; Yuling and his friend Xu Mengrong would not attach themselves to him and were slandered by him; Yuling was moved to Junior Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi of Jingzhao then enjoyed imperial favor and ruled by terror. Yuling and his friend Xu Mengrong refused to join his faction and were slandered; Yuling was transferred to junior director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，宣遺詔於太原、幽州，節府獻遺無所納。

translations.literal: When the emperor died he proclaimed the death edict at Taiyuan and Youzhou; the military commissions offered gifts which he accepted none of.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, he was sent to proclaim the testament at Taiyuan and Youzhou and accepted none of the gifts the frontier commands offered.

sentences.zh: 拜華州刺史，遷浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Hua Prefecture and transferred to Inspector of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Hua Prefecture, then inspector of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 越人饑，請出米三十萬石扌烝贍貧民，政聲流聞。

translations.literal: The Yue people were starving; he requested to release three hundred thousand shi of grain to relieve and support the poor; his reputation for governance spread.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the Yue region he asked to release three hundred thousand shi of grain to relieve the poor, and his reputation for good government spread far.

sentences.zh: 入為京兆尹。

translations.literal: He entered service as Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 先是，編民多竄北軍籍中，倚以橫閭裏。

translations.literal: Previously, registered commoners often hid themselves in Northern Army rolls and relied on this to tyrannize their neighborhoods.
translations.idiomatic: Previously many registered residents had slipped into Northern Army rolls and used that cover to bully their neighborhoods.

sentences.zh: 於陵請限丁制，減三丁者不得著籍，奸人無所影賴，京師豪右大震。

translations.literal: Yuling requested a limit on household rolls: households reduced by three adult males could not register; scoundrels had nowhere to hide; the capital's powerful were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Yuling proposed a household quota: families missing three adult males could not enlist; with nowhere to hide, the capital's bully magnates quaked.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice-Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice-Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 元和初，牛僧孺等以賢良方正對策，於陵被詔程其文，居第一，宰相惡其言，出為嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, Niu Sengru and others answered on the theme Incorruptible and Upright; Yuling was ordered by edict to grade their essays and placed Niu first; the chief minister disliked his words and sent Yuling out as military governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yuanhe, Niu Sengru and others took the incorrupt-and-upright examination; Yuling was ordered to grade the papers and ranked Niu first. The chief minister hated Niu's answers and had Yuling posted as military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 辟韋詞、李翺等在幕府，咨訪得失，教民陶瓦易蒲屋，以絕火患。

translations.literal: He recruited Wei Ci, Li Ao, and others to his staff, consulted them on gain and loss, and taught the people to fire tiles and replace rush-roofed houses to eliminate fire hazards.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited Wei Ci, Li Ao, and others to his staff, sought their counsel on policy, and taught the people to fire roof tiles and replace thatched cottages—eliminating a major source of fires.

sentences.zh: 監軍許遂振者，悍戾貪肆，憚於陵，不敢撓以私，則為飛語聞京師，憲宗不能無惑，有詔罷歸。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Xu Suizhen was fierce, cruel, greedy, and unrestrained; he feared Yuling and dared not interfere for private ends, so he spread flying rumors heard in the capital; Xianzong could not but be swayed, and an edict recalled Yuling.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor Xu Suizhen was brutal, greedy, and overbearing. He feared Yuling and dared not push private interests, so he fed rumors to the capital. Even Xianzong wavered, and Yuling was recalled by edict.

sentences.zh: 遂振領留事，笞吏剔抉其贓，吏呼曰：「楊公尚拒他方賂遺，肯私官錢邪？」

translations.literal: Suizhen took charge of remaining affairs, flogged clerks and picked out their graft; a clerk cried: "Even Lord Yang rejected bribes from other places—would he steal official funds?"
translations.idiomatic: Suizhen took over local affairs and tortured clerks to extract evidence of embezzlement. One clerk cried, "Lord Yang would refuse even gifts from outsiders—would he steal public funds?"

sentences.zh: 宰相裴垍亦為帝別白言之，乃授吏部侍郎，而遂振終得罪。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Pei Ji also explained separately to the emperor, and Yuling was then appointed Vice-Minister of Personnel; Suizhen ultimately met with punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Pei Ji cleared the matter for the emperor, and Yuling was appointed Vice-Minister of Personnel; Xu Suizhen eventually met his downfall.

sentences.zh: 初，吏部程判，別詔官參考，齊抗當國，罷之。

translations.literal: Originally the Ministry of Personnel's grading of examination results had a separately edicted reviewing officer; when Qi Kang held power it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Ministry of Personnel's grading had been reviewed by separately appointed officials, but when Qi Kang ran the government that practice was abolished.

sentences.zh: 至是，尚書鄭餘慶移疾，乃循舊制。

translations.literal: At this time the Minister Zheng Yuqing reported illness and submitted resignation, and the old system was followed.
translations.idiomatic: By then Minister Zheng Yuqing took medical leave, and the old review system was restored.

sentences.zh: 於陵建言：「他官但第判能否，不知限員，有司計員為留遣之格，事不相謀，莫如勿置。」

translations.literal: Yu Ling memorialized: "Other offices only grade on ability or inability and do not know quota limits; the relevant offices count quotas as the standard for retention or dismissal—the matters are not coordinated; it would be better not to set such quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ling proposed: "Other offices judge only whether candidates are capable, without regard to quota limits, while the responsible bureaus use head counts as the rule for keeping or releasing men—the two processes do not work together. It would be better to abolish the quota system altogether.

sentences.zh: 於是有詔三考官止較科目選，至常調悉還吏部。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the three examination officers to compare only examination-route selections, while all regular transfers were fully returned to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: the three examination officers were to evaluate only examination-route candidates, and all routine transfers were returned entirely to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 又請修甲歷，南曹置別簿相檢實，吏不能為奸。

translations.literal: He also requested revision of rank registers; the Southern Office kept separate ledgers for mutual verification, so clerks could not commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that service registers be brought up to date and that the Southern Office keep separate ledgers for cross-checking, so that clerks could no longer cheat.

sentences.zh: 始奏選者納直給符告，居四年，凡調三千員，時謂為適。

translations.literal: He first had selected candidates pay a fee to receive appointment documents; over four years roughly three thousand posts were filled through transfer—contemporaries considered this appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: He first required successful candidates to pay a fee before receiving their appointment notices. Over four years some three thousand posts were filled through transfer, and contemporaries regarded the pace as about right.

sentences.zh: 以兵部兼御史大夫，判度支。

translations.literal: As Minister of War he also served as Chief Censor with charge of the Commission for Public Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of War while also holding the post of Chief Censor and taking charge of the revenue commission.

sentences.zh: 王師討淮西，於陵用所親為供軍使，主唐、鄧，而高霞寓騰牒度支，以餉道乏。

translations.literal: When imperial troops campaigned against Huai West, Yu Ling appointed a close associate as army supply commissioner in charge of Tang and Deng; Gao Xiayu sent urgent dispatches to the revenue commission complaining of exhausted supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial armies marched against Huai West, Yu Ling put a close associate in charge of army supplies for Tang and Deng prefectures. Gao Xiayu sent urgent dispatches to the revenue commission reporting that the supply lines were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 及戰敗，詔責之，指以為言。

translations.literal: When battle was lost, an edict held him responsible, citing this as the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was defeated, an edict censured him and cited this very matter as the cause.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，貶於陵郴州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted Yu Ling to prefect of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and demoted Yu Ling to prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 徙原王傅，復以戶部侍郎知吏部選。

translations.literal: He was transferred to tutor of the Prince of Yuan and again served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue with charge of personnel selection.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to tutor of the Prince of Yuan and again served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue with charge of personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 李師道平，詔宣慰淄青。

translations.literal: When Li Shidao was suppressed, an edict ordered Yu Ling to console Zi and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Shidao was pacified, an edict appointed Yu Ling commissioner of consolation to Zi and Qing.

sentences.zh: 朝廷始議分其地，而劉悟節度滑州，未出鄆，於陵趣使上道。

translations.literal: The court had begun discussing partition of the territory; Liu Wu held command at Hua Prefecture but had not yet left Yan. Yu Ling urged him to set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The court had just begun debating how to divide the territory. Liu Wu was military commissioner at Hua Prefecture but had not yet departed from Yan. Yu Ling pressed him to take to the road at once.

sentences.zh: 還奏，帝悅其能。

translations.literal: On returning he reported; the emperor was pleased with his capability.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned and reported, the emperor was pleased with his competence.

sentences.zh: 會浙西觀察使李閹死，皇甫镈素忌於陵，薦以代翛，帝不之可。

translations.literal: When observation commissioner Li Yan of Zhexi died, Huangfu Bo, who had long resented Yu Ling, recommended him to replace Xiao; the emperor did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yan, observation commissioner of Zhexi, died, Huangfu Bo—who had long resented Yu Ling—recommended him as replacement. The emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，遷戶部尚書，為東都留守。

translations.literal: When Muzong acceded, Yu Ling was promoted to Minister of Revenue and made eastern capital garrison commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Yu Ling was promoted to Minister of Revenue and appointed garrison commissioner of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 數上疏乞身，不許。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized asking to retire, but permission was not granted.

sentences.zh: 授太子少傅，封弘農郡公。

translations.literal: He was granted Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 俄以尚書左仆射致仕，詔賜實俸，讓不受。

translations.literal: Soon he retired as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; an edict granted him full salary but he declined to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired with the title Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. An edict granted him his full salary, but he declined to accept it.

sentences.zh: 於陵器量方峻，進止有常度，節操堅明，始終不失其正，時人尊仰之。

translations.literal: Yu Ling's bearing was stern and square; his conduct had constant measure; his integrity was firm and bright; from beginning to end he never lost his rectitude; contemporaries honored and looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ling was stern and upright in bearing, measured in all he did, and firm and clear in integrity. He never lost his rectitude from first to last, and his contemporaries honored and revered him.

sentences.zh: 太和四年卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Taihe, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Taihe (830), at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 冊贈司空，謚曰貞孝。

translations.literal: Posthumously invested as Grand Tutor; posthumous epithet Zhenxiao (Upright and Filial).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously invested as Grand Tutor and given the posthumous name Upright and Filial.

sentences.zh: 四子：景復仕至同州刺史，紹復中書舍人，師復大理卿，中子嗣復位宰相，自有傳。

translations.literal: Four sons: Jingfu rose to prefect of Tong Prefecture; Shaofu became Secretariat Drafter; Shifu became Minister of Justice; the middle son Sifu reached the chancellorship and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Jingfu rose to prefect of Tongzhou; Shaofu became Secretariat Drafter; Shifu became Minister of Justice; and the middle son Sifu reached the chancellorship and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 馬總，字會元，系出扶風。

translations.literal: Ma Zong, courtesy name Huiyuan, traced his descent to Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zong, styled Huiyuan, came from the Fufeng line of the Ma clan.

sentences.zh: 少孤窶，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and impoverished, he did not associate with others recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, he did not make friends lightly.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，辟署滑州姚南仲幕府，監軍薛盈珍誣南仲不法，總坐貶泉州別駕。

translations.literal: During Zhenyuan he was invited to Yao Nanzong's staff in Hua Prefecture. Army supervisor Xue Yingzhen falsely accused Nanzong of lawlessness, and Zong was implicated and demoted to vice prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era (785–804) he joined Yao Nanzong's staff in Huazhou. Army supervisor Xue Yingzhen falsely accused Nanzong of misconduct, and Zong was implicated and demoted to vice prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 盈珍入用事，福建觀察使柳冕希旨欲誅之，會刺史穆贊保護，乃免。

translations.literal: When Yingzhen entered court power, Fujian observation commissioner Liu Mian, eager to please, wished to execute him; fortunately prefect Mu Zan protected him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzhen came to power at court, Fujian observation commissioner Liu Mian, eager to curry favor, tried to have him executed. Prefect Mu Zan protected him, and he escaped death.

sentences.zh: 徙恩王傅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to tutor of the Prince of En.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to tutor of the Prince of En.

sentences.zh: 元和中，以虔州刺史遷安南都護，廉清不撓，用儒術教其俗，政事嘉美，獠夷安之。

translations.literal: During Yuanhe, promoted from prefect of Qian to Protector-General of Annan, he was incorrupt and unyielding, taught the people with Confucian methods, governance was excellent, and the Liao and Yi peoples were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era (806–820) he was promoted from prefect of Qianzhou to Protector-General of Annan. Incorruptible and unyielding, he taught the people with Confucian learning, his administration was exemplary, and the tribal peoples were brought to peace.

sentences.zh: 建二銅柱於漢故處，镵著唐德，以明伏波之裔。

translations.literal: He erected two bronze columns at the old Han site, inscribed with Tang virtue, to show descent from the Marquis of Fubo.
translations.idiomatic: He erected two bronze columns at the old Han site, inscribed with Tang virtue, to proclaim descent from the Marquis Who Pacified the Waves.

sentences.zh: 徙桂管經略觀察使，入為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Transferred to Guangxi military commissioner and observation commissioner; entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner and observation commissioner of Guangxi, then entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 十二年，兼御史大夫，副裴度宣慰淮西。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he also served as Chief Censor, assisting Pei Du in consoling Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was additionally appointed Chief Censor and served as Pei Du's deputy in pacifying Huai West.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟禽，為彰義節度留後。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanji was captured, he served as acting military commissioner of Zhangyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji was captured, Zong was made acting military commissioner of Zhangyi.

sentences.zh: 蔡人習偽惡，相掉訐，獷戾有夷貊風。

translations.literal: The people of Cai were accustomed to deceit and wickedness, slandering one another, fierce and brutal with the air of barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Cai were steeped in deceit and malice, denouncing one another, fierce and unruly with the manners of frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 總為設教令，明賞罰，磨治洗汰，其俗一變。

translations.literal: Zong established teachings and orders, clarified rewards and punishments, polished and cleansed them, and their customs were wholly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Zong established rules and teachings, made rewards and punishments clear, and through steady reform and purging transformed their customs entirely.

sentences.zh: 始奏改彰義為淮西，尋擢拜淮西節度使，徙忠武，改華州防禦、鎮國軍使。

translations.literal: He first memorialized to change Zhangyi to Huai West, was soon appointed military commissioner of Huai West, transferred to Zhongwu, then changed to Hua Prefecture defense commissioner and commander of the Zhenguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: He first memorialized to rename Zhangyi as Huai West, was soon appointed its military commissioner, then transferred to Zhongwu, and later became defense commissioner of Huazhou and commander of the Zhenguo Army.

sentences.zh: 李師道平，析鄆、曹、濮等為一道，除總節度，賜號天平軍。

translations.literal: When Li Shidao was pacified, Yan, Cao, Pu and others were carved out as one circuit; Zong was appointed commissioner and granted the title Pingjun Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shidao was pacified, Yan, Cao, Pu, and neighboring prefectures were organized into a new circuit. Zong was appointed its commissioner and the army was named Tianping.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，劉總上幽、鎮地，詔總徙天平，而召揔還，將大用之。

translations.literal: At the start of Changqing Liu Zong offered up You and Zhen territories; an edict moved Zong to Tianping and recalled Zong intending to employ him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Changqing (821), Liu Zong surrendered the You and Zhen territories. An edict moved Ma Zong to Tianping and recalled Liu Zong to court, intending to give him high office.

sentences.zh: 會總卒，穆宗以鄆人附賴總，復詔還鎮。

translations.literal: When Zong died, Muzong because the Yan people relied on Zong, again ordered him to return to his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zong died, Emperor Muzong, knowing the people of Yan relied on Ma Zong, ordered him back to his command.

sentences.zh: 二年，檢校尚書左仆射，入為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year, acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; entered court as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and entered court as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 總篤學，雖吏事倥傯，書不去前，論著頗多。

translations.literal: Zong was devoted to learning; though buried in administrative affairs, his books never left his desk, and he wrote many treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was deeply devoted to learning. Though overwhelmed with administrative work, he always kept books before him and produced many scholarly writings.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈右仆射，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Right Vice Director; posthumous epithet Yi (Solemn).
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the posthumous name Solemn.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：巢父恃正義，觸群不肖，謀不以權，遂喪其身。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Chaofu relied on righteousness, offended many unworthy men, and did not use stratagem to his advantage; thus he lost his life.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Chaofu stood on righteousness, provoked many unworthy men, and would not use cunning to his advantage—thus he lost his life.

sentences.zh: 寧、邠皆所謂邦之司直者，後世卒蕃衍。

translations.literal: Ning and Bin were both what is called direct correctors of the state; their descendants in later generations flourished and multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Ning and Bin were both what the ancients called the state's straight correctors, and their lines flourished and multiplied in later generations.

sentences.zh: 公綽仁而勇，於陵方重，總沈懿，皆有大臣風，才堪宰相而用不至，果時有不幸邪？

translations.literal: Gongchuo was benevolent yet brave, Yu Ling was square and weighty, Zong was deep and solemn—all had the bearing of great ministers, talent fit for the chancellorship yet not brought to that use; was it truly that the times brought misfortune?
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo was benevolent and brave, Yu Ling was upright and weighty, and Zong was deep and solemn—all had the bearing of great ministers and talent fit for the chancellorship, yet never reached that office. Was it truly that the times were against them?

sentences.zh: 穆、崔、柳代為孝友聞家，君子之澤遠哉！

translations.literal: The Mu, Cui, and Liu families in succession were famed households of filial piety and brotherly love—how far the beneficence of the gentleman extends!
translations.idiomatic: The Mu, Cui, and Liu clans in succession were renowned for filial piety and brotherly devotion—how far the gentleman's beneficence reaches!
